item.title: Modi's predicament: Gen Z pours out on India's streets as dissent surges
item.description: Despite tens of thousands of security personnel deployed to stop them, youth protesters in India scaled barricades last week, chanted anti-government slogans and scuffled with police officers trying to drag them away.
item.dc:creator: Tora Agarwala, Saurabh Sharma, Sunil Kataria
item.content:encoded: Despite tens of thousands of security personnel deployed to stop them, youth protesters in India scaled barricades last week, chanted anti-government slogans and scuffled with police officers trying to drag them away. "Long live the revolution," shouted one young man before police bundled him into a bus. Street protests in India this year are likely to be higher than at any time in the past decade, the independent Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) Project has said, as dissent mounts against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and Gen Z activists pour on to the streets. Analysts say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014, with people under 30 making up nearly one quarter of the country's 1 billion voters. But his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029. "The nation has suddenly found its voice," said Yogendra Yadav, an anti-government activist who has played a leading part in the demonstrations. "I would not say this is the beginning of the end of the Modi regime, but this definitely is the beginning of a downward spiral". The government and Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party declined comment for this story. The recent protests in the capital Delhi and elsewhere were focused on demands that Election Commission chief [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] resign over a [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"voter roll revision"] that activists and opposition parties say favours the BJP and has helped it win several recent state elections. The ruling BJP, the government and the Election Commission deny the accusations. The BJP says the party's wins have come from Modi's popularity and strong economic growth. But the demonstrations are also reflecting something larger: growing anger at Modi for failing to deliver jobs to millions of unemployed youth in his 12 years in power despite the surge in headline economic growth. Other issues have also fed into the anti-establishment mood, including leaks of question papers in [USN:L4N43O0C9 TEXT:"key examinations"] for jobs and education, the high number of crimes against women and the rise of billionaire businessmen alleged to have close links to Modi. Modi has a strongman image and his government has previously cracked down on pockets of dissent harshly, but that hasn't fazed the youngsters on the streets. "The fear in us is gone," said Ananya Raturi, a 21-year-old Delhi University student who was part of massive protests in the capital on Saturday. Speaking after she clung to the windscreen wipers of a bus that police were using to detain protesters, Raturi said: "We don't fear being detained or beaten up by the police. This generation enjoys it." Police have denied allegations that they beat up people at the demonstrations, saying protesters were handled according to prescribed procedures. THE RISE OF THE COCKROACHES The protests have been energised by the emergence of the first nationally resonant youth-led movement of the Modi era, the [USN:L4N45W00W TEXT:"Cockroach Janta Party"], which grew from online satire into a nationwide campaign this June after India's chief justice likened the unemployed to "cockroaches". India's mainstream media is mostly pro-government, critics say, and has covered the protests sparingly. But thousands of protesters armed with mobile phones as well as independent news channels on YouTube have amplified the unrest and made Internet stars of leaders like CJP founder [USN:L1N45W01X TEXT:"Abhijeet Dipke"] and firebrand left-wing activist [USN:L4N45X011 TEXT:"Neha Bora"]. Opposition parties that were subdued under Modi's grip on power have been re-energised, with Congress Party leader Rahul Gandhi and tens of thousands of followers also on the streets. The unrest has drawn comparisons with neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal, where youth-led protest movements brought down governments in recent years, although analysts caution that India's political landscape and Modi's popularity make such parallels imperfect. Many of the youth protesters grew up during Modi's rise to power, buoyed by promises of jobs, opportunity and cleaner governance. A decade later, many say those aspirations remain unfulfilled and they say the Hindu nationalist government appears more focused on religious issues and divisive politics against minorities, especially Muslims. The government has previously said the economy generated 168.3 million new jobs in the six years through 2024. Modi has repeatedly rejected allegations of any bias, saying his government works for all Indians. 30-year-old Gauri Seth, a medical student based in Kolkata, became a voter in 2014, the same year the Modi government came to power. Seth said the Modi government promised "a lot, but has failed to deliver." "Instead they focus on things like religious infrastructure. There are cases of violence against minorities. When anyone speaks against them, it is labelled as treason or sedition." IT'S MOSTLY ABOUT JOBS When Modi came to power, he promised the creation of millions of jobs each year. Yet, despite India's strong economic growth since then, unemployment remains at slightly above 5%, according to government data. A Reuters poll last year said that data masks the [USN:L4N3TC0XX TEXT:"severity of joblessness"], especially among the youth. Unemployment among the 367 million people in the country aged 15-29 stood at 9.9% in 2025, according to the data. Research by Azim Premji University's State of Working India 2026 report found unemployment among graduates aged 15-25 was nearly 40%, while about one in five graduates aged 25-29 remained jobless. In May, unrest erupted across the country when the government invalidated examinations for national medical colleges, a pathway to jobs for the poor and the middle class , after test papers were leaked. Rubby Singh, a 30-year-old social activist in Delhi, said repeated examination paper leaks had deepened a sense among young Indians that the system was denying them opportunities even after years of study. "This generation has been facing the brunt of not having proper education, which leads to not being able to get good opportunities," she said. While national elections are not due for almost three years, the country's biggest state, Uttar Pradesh, goes to the polls early next year, which could provide a test of Modi's popularity. Analysts however remain cautious about the outcome. The BJP may not be as strong as it was a few months ago, said Rahul Verma, a fellow at the Centre for Policy Research in New Delhi. "But whether there are going to be electoral implications, it is too early to say."

item.title: Brewers rally to sweep Dodgers, earn first World Series bid since '82
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Jake Bauers started the Brewers' comeback with a two-run double and Garrett Mitchell hit a go-ahead home run to deliver a 6-4 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday and send Milwaukee to its first World Series appearance in 44 years.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- Jake Bauers started the Brewers' comeback with a two-run double and Garrett Mitchell hit a go-ahead home run to deliver a 6-4 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday and send Milwaukee to its first World Series appearance in 44 years. Bauers added a bases-loaded walk to tie the game in the fifth inning as the Brewers rallied from an early four-run deficit to sweep the National League Championship Series in four games. The dominating performance came after Milwaukee was swept out of the NLCS by Los Angeles last season. Catcher William Contreras guided the Brewers' pitching staff in a bullpen game, and four pitchers held the Dodgers scoreless over the final seven innings. JoJo Romero (2-1) tossed two innings, and Aaron Ashby handled the final three frames for his second save of the postseason. Bauers was selected the Most Valuable Player of the NLCS after going 4-for-14 (.286) with one homer and six RBIs. The Brewers will open the World Series at home on Oct. 23 against the winner of the American League Championship Series between the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays. The Guardians hold a 2-1 lead after winning 3-2 on Thursday. Milwaukee made its only previous World Series appearance as an AL team in 1982, falling in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals. Shohei Ohtani hit a three-run homer in his return to the leadoff spot but also struck out three times while playing with knee and biceps discomfort that will be addressed in the offseason. Dodgers starter Tyler Glasnow gave up four runs on three hits and two walks over 4 1/3 innings. He struck out six. Tanner Scott (0-1) gave up Mitchell's go-ahead home run in the sixth inning. The Dodgers appeared to be all business in the second inning when Andy Pages delivered a one-out RBI single and Ohtani added a towering three-run blast with two outs for a 4-0 advantage. Bauers continued his impressive series in the fourth inning with a two-run ground-rule double to cut the Milwaukee deficit in half. David Hamilton pulled the Brewers within 4-3 in the fifth inning with an RBI single, ending Glasnow's outing. Dodgers reliever Evan Phillips subsequently loaded the bases with two outs on a pair of walks. Alex Vesia replaced Phillips and walked Bauers on four pitches to tie the game. Milwaukee went up for good in the sixth at 5-4 when Mitchell, a Southern California native and UCLA alumnus, greeted Scott with a leadoff home run. The Dodgers wasted a one-out double from Kyle Tucker in the sixth inning and a leadoff double from Pages in the seventh. Another double combined with an error in the eighth put Will Smith on third base as the tying run with one out. Ashby then retired Tucker on a shallow fly ball and struck out Teoscar Hernandez to end the threat. Hamilton sealed the victory with a two-out home run in the ninth inning against Edwin Diaz. --Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.title: Global fuel oil market stays tight as conflicts hit Mideast, Russia supplies, Vitol says
item.description: A resumption of hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz is supporting high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) premiums as supplies remain tight on lower exports from the Middle East and Russia while bunker demand stays robust, Vitol's Asia head said.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: A resumption of hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz is supporting high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) premiums as supplies remain tight on lower exports from the Middle East and Russia while bunker demand stays robust, Vitol's Asia head said. HSFO flows through Hormuz, including Iranian supplies, remain down by at least 800,000 metric tons per month from February, Kieran Gallagher said at the Singapore International Bunker conference (SIBCON) this week. Exports via Hormuz averaged about 3.7 million tons a month between January 2025 and February 2026, Kpler data showed. While the volume improves on the 2 million tons loss in May, attacks on Russian refineries have led to an additional estimated monthly loss of 1 million tons of fuel oil, he added. Spot premiums for 380-cst HSFO hovered near $50 a ton this week versus a $5.10 premium on February 27, LSEG data showed. "Producers are paying higher freight rates and more risk premiums to shuttle cargoes out of Hormuz, recognising the importance of oil revenues to their national budgets," Gallagher said. However, attacks on shipping and oil infrastructure remain a threat, putting at risk supplies that the market currently assumes will be available, he added. Some North Asian refiners have switched to processing fuel oil at their upgrading units instead of crude, drawing more than 1 million tons of HSFO for November, after recent disruptions to Saudi Arabia's crude exports from the Red Sea, Gallagher said. "The key lies in replacing fuel oil with crude as a refinery feedstock," he added. By contrast, conditions in the low-sulphur fuel oil market are more benign, he said, pointing to higher exports from China and Nigeria's Dangote refinery, which is exporting two to three Suezmax-sized cargoes a month. MORE BUNKERING OPTIONS In response to the Middle East disruption, Vitol [USN:FWN43G0JC TEXT:"began bunkering"] at Pakistan's Gwadar Port in July, offering an alternative to United Arab Emirates' Fujairah, which lies just outside the Strait of Hormuz, to serve customers operating in the Gulf region. The world's largest independent oil trader, Vitol delivers about 15 million tons of bunker fuel per year and is also diversifying the types of fuels it can supply to shippers. Vitol expects to start liquefied natural gas deliveries in Singapore in coming weeks and is also keen to explore opportunities to supply bio-LNG, Gallagher said. Vitol expects to receive an LNG bunker vessel in November and two more next year. Singapore's January-to-September 2026 LNG bunker sales totalled 487,100 tons, up more than 21% from a year earlier, data from the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore showed Wednesday. "That growth has continued against a challenging backdrop," Gallagher said.

item.title: Mideast war alters global bunker buying patterns, industry execs say
item.description: The US-Israeli war on Iran has altered bunker buying patterns for shippers globally as they turned to more spot and shorter-term purchases to cope with volatile prices while exploring more alternative locations for supply security, industry executives said.
item.dc:creator: Jeslyn Lerh
item.content:encoded: The US-Israeli war on Iran has altered bunker buying patterns for shippers globally as they turned to more spot and shorter-term purchases to cope with volatile prices while exploring more alternative locations for supply security, industry executives said. More than seven months since the start of the conflict with Iran, prices of marine fuels remained well over 70% versus pre-war levels, according to data from bunker traders. Rerouting and diversions of vessels due to blockades at key waterways in the Middle East have also driven shippers to diversify refuelling locations, making them less inclined to lock in a longer-term contracts at one particular port, the executives said. "The frequency of stems (spot purchases) is getting higher because a lot of owners will bunker the minimum to reach the next port if the market shoots up," said Peter Grunwaldt, chief executive officer at Seascale Energy and head of bunkering at tanker company Hafnia, on the sidelines of the Singapore International Bunkering conference. Spot purchases give more flexibility to the shipowner, who decides whether to buy bunkers in that instance, depending on the daily price, suppliers said. In contrast, if they lock into a longer term contract, they will have to lift the agreed volume regardless of how the price swings. "When prices are elevated, you have this notion that if prices fall tomorrow, you don't want to be too exposed," said Mikkel Kannegaard, chief operating officer at Bunker Holding, the world's largest bunker seller by volume. "So we have seen a trend where longer-term contracts have become less common," he told Reuters, adding that bunker trade has become more complex amid a more fragmented market. Choong Zhen Mao, executive director at Singapore-based [USN:L1N4600CW TEXT:"Equatorial Marine Fuel"], said the duration of term contracts with buyers had shortened to a quarter or even a month, versus longer terms like six months or one year, before the war. ALTERNATIVE BUNKER PORTS Besides breaking up the size of bunker purchases, shippers are also turning to alternative locations to seek bunker supplies and refuel as hostilities around the United Arab Emirates' Fujairah port, which used to be a top supplier, intensified, the executives said. "Around the Arabian Gulf in particular, traditional bunkering patterns are being torn apart," said Seascale's Grunwaldt. "Diversions from Fujairah have clearly driven more enquiries to surrounding ports, so we now bunker in more ports than we used to," he added. "Ports that were only used sporadically before, such as Port Louis, Colombo and Salalah, are now being used more frequently," he said, referring to ports in Mauritius, Sri Lanka and Oman. [USN:L4N45V0MF TEXT:"Bunker Holding"]'s Kannegaard said he had seen more demand emerging in Africa and South Asia. In response to the Middle East disruption, Vitol [USN:FWN43G0JC TEXT:"began bunkering"] at the Gwadar Port in Pakistan in July, offering a location outside the Strait of Hormuz from which to serve customers operating in the Gulf region. "Diversification is essential, both to manage today's disruptions and to build longer-term resilience," Vitol's Head of Asia Kieran Gallagher said. "In the near term, that means broadening geographic sources of supply and developing new trade routes for conventional fuels."

item.title: Kiss confident Nawaqanitawase will return to the Wallabies fold
item.description: Australia coach Les Kiss is confident Mark Nawaqanitawase will return to the Wallabies after his two-year stint in rugby league but warned the athletic winger would have to earn his spot in the team.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia coach Les Kiss is confident Mark Nawaqanitawase will return to the Wallabies after his two-year stint in rugby league but warned the athletic winger would have to earn his spot in the team. Nawaqanitawase finished up his spell with the Sydney Roosters after his tries helped them to the National Rugby League (NRL) [USN:L4N45Q016 TEXT:"title"] earlier this month and is returning to the 15-man game on a two-year deal with Japan's Wild Knights. The 26-year-old's agent Milan Volavola-Shankar [USN:L4N45Z0F5 TEXT:"said"] on Tuesday that there was no guarantee Nawaqanitawase would play for the Wallabies again given he would also qualify to play for Fiji or Italy from midway through next year. Kiss said he accepted that Nawaqanitawase would not be available for November's Nations Championship games in Europe but thought he would be back in the green and gold of Australia before next year's World Cup on home soil. "We've had a couple of chats and (we were) always waiting for the end of the year to see where he sits," Kiss told reporters on Thursday after naming his team for this weekend's clash with the All Blacks. "He's had a big year, a fantastic year, hasn't he? So the conversations are being wrapped around making sure we get what's right for him. "I think there's no doubt that you know he wants to be back in the game for us, that's for sure," Kiss added. "So we'll continue our conversations and go from there. I'm not going to speak on his behalf. That's all. But we know where he wants to play." Kiss, himself a former rugby league winger, said Nawaqanitawase would need some time to readjust to rugby union and was not certain to come straight back into the Australia side. "Everyone will earn their way," he said. "But if he's playing good footy, he'll be in the mix, that's for sure. There's no doubt he's a quality player that we'll keep an eye on. "He'll have some opportunities but first and foremost, (he needs to) get his rest, get himself together and get into some rugby back in Japan. "It's a different game in terms of height and how you attack the game, how you move in the game, how you defend, how the aerial game is different, so he's got a lot of things just to relearn. "Won't take him long, that's for sure." Nawaqanitawase made 11 appearances for the Wallabies before switching to the NRL, where he built a reputation as one of the game's biggest aerial threats as well as someone able to conjure up stunning tries.

item.title: Philippines hits back at Chinese envoy over 'thinly veiled threat' of force
item.description: The Philippines has chided China's ambassador for what it interpreted as a "thinly veiled threat" of force, after Beijing's envoy said his country would prevail in a confrontation between them.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philippines has chided China's ambassador for what it interpreted as a "thinly veiled threat" of force, after Beijing's envoy said his country would prevail in a confrontation between them. The Philippine foreign ministry said ambassador Jing Quan's remarks to journalists on Thursday were a "poor choice of words" and unhelpful given their complicated bilateral ties Jing had said China "may easily win" but would not use force as "we love peace" The ambassador was asked for his reaction to the Philippine defence secretary calling China a regional "troublemaker" Their comments were the latest heated exchange between China and US defence ally the Philippines, which have repeatedly sparred over disputed features in the South China Sea Asked on Friday about the ambassador's remarks, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said it "sounds very much like a threat" deserving of a discussion with the envoy The Chinese Embassy said the ambassador had been selectively quoted and called Manila's response an "over-interpretation", adding relations were currently "at an extremely sensitive stage" The Philippines and China have been at loggerheads for years over reefs and islands in the South China Sea located in the Philippine exclusive economic zone, with their coast guards squaring off repeatedly

item.title: Japan core inflation likely exceeded BOJ target for first time since December
item.description: Japan's core consumer inflation in September likely exceeded the central bank's 2% target as higher energy prices driven by the Middle East conflict fed through to households, a Reuters poll showed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan's core consumer inflation in September likely exceeded the central bank's 2% target as higher energy prices driven by the Middle East conflict fed through to households, a Reuters poll showed on Friday. The nationwide core consumer price index (CPI), which includes energy items but excludes fresh food prices, is expected to have risen 2.1% in September from a year earlier, according to a poll of 15 economists That would mark an acceleration from 1.7% in August and put core inflation above the Bank of Japan's 2% target for the first time since December "Amid the emerging deterioration of the situation in Iran, growth is expected to accelerate for food items excluding rice as well as daily necessities," said Ryosuke Katagi, a market economist at Mizuho Securities Separate [USN:L4N45Y1EW TEXT:"data"] released on Tuesday showed Japan's wholesale inflation rose 6.8% year-on-year in September, slowing from the previous month but underscoring persistent price pressures that continue to fuel market expectations of a near-term BOJ rate hike The BOJ may signal this month that underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2% target, highlighting its readiness to raise interest rates again in the coming months. But many in the central bank are wary of hiking again at its October 29-30 policy meeting The internal affairs ministry will release CPI data at 8:30 a.m. on Friday, October 23 (2330 GMT on October 22)

item.title: Wild ride Matt Boldy’s hat trick to win over Blues
item.description: Matt Boldy scored his fifth career hat trick and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild held off the St. Louis Blues 5-4 Thursday night in Saint Paul, Minn.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Matt Boldy scored his fifth career hat trick and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild held off the St. Louis Blues 5-4 Thursday night in Saint Paul, Minn. Kirill Kaprizov scored his third goal in two games and added two assists for the Wild, who have won three of four. Quinn Hughes and Joel Eriksson Ek each had two assists and Jesper Wallstedt made 20 saves. Kaprizov, who has 11 points (six goals, five assists) during a five-game point streak, headed to the dressing room late in the third period after being pushed into the boards by Hofer. Robert Thomas had a goal and an assist, and Mason McTavish scored his third goal in two games for the Blues, ending their three-game point streak (2-0-1). Cam Fowler had three assists, and Joel Hofer made 33 saves. Trailing 5-2, the Blues pulled within 5-3 on Thomas' short-handed goal at 16:00 of the third period, and Dylan Holloway made it 5-4 with 15 seconds remaining. Jonatan Berggren gave the Blues a 1-0 lead 1:45 into the game when he received a pass below the goal line, skated into the slot and lifted a backhand shot past Wallstedt on the power play. Boldy tied it at 7:31 during a 5-on-3 power play, scoring on a one-timer from the high slot off a pass from Hughes, who has an eight-game assist streak. Danila Yurov put Minnesota ahead 2-1 on a one-timer from the edge of the right circle off a centering pass from Maxim Shabanov on a 3-on-2 rush at 11:17. McTavish tied it 2-2 at 4:57 of the second period when a lob pass from Pius Suter sent him in alone and he slid the puck through the five hole. The tie lasted just 27 seconds before Boldy took a pass from Eriksson Ek behind the goal line and beat Hofer with a wrist shot from the right circle at 5:24. Kaprizov made it 4-2 when he tipped in Hughes' centering attempt at 8:47. Boldy completed his hat trick with his fifth goal of the season at 16:47, scoring on a one-timer from the left circle off a pass from Kaprizov in the corner to increase the lead to 5-2. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blackhawks hold on for overtime win despite Jets' comeback
item.description: Artyom Levshunov scored 97 seconds into overtime for the Chicago Blackhawks, who beat the Winnipeg Jets 4-3 to win their second straight game.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Artyom Levshunov scored 97 seconds into overtime for the Chicago Blackhawks, who beat the Winnipeg Jets 4-3 to win their second straight game. The Russian defenseman, the second overall pick in the 2024 NHL Draft, got his third career goal and first in OT on a backhand pass from Connor Bedard to the high slot. Bedard, in his second game of the season, scored a power-play goal, and Patrick Kane assisted on both. Frank Nazar scored a goal in his first game for Chicago after serving a two-game suspension for an illegal head check last week, and Ryan Donato tallied his second of the season. Spencer Knight made 31 saves. His biggest was his last, as his outstretched pad save kept Winnipeg's Neal Pionk from winning the game and allowed the Blackhawks to set up their game-winning rush. Pionk finished with a goal and two assists as Winnipeg rallied from down two after a period to get a point. Kyle Connor extended his goal-scoring streak to four games, and Alex Iafallo got his second of the season. Stuart Skinner stopped 24 shots and the Jets have earned at least a point in each of his five games. The Blackhawks started as the more aggressive team and finally broke through thanks to a 5-on-3 power play. Bedard's goal with 11:49 left -- and two seconds left on the two-man advantage -- came off a give-and-go with Kane. That assist was the 895th of Kane's career, allowing him to supplant Phil Housley for the most by an American in the NHL. Nazar doubled the home team's advantage nearly seven minutes later after a rebound of a shot from the point by Winnipeg's Jack St. Ivany skidded into the neutral zone and created a breakaway opportunity. Pionk answered for Winnipeg, with a slap shot from the point got redirected by Ethan Del Mastro's stick with 3:03 remaining. However, Donato needed just 14 seconds to make it 3-1. Chicago outshot Winnipeg 14-8 in the opening period, but the Jets controlled the final 40 minutes of regulation. Connor cut the deficit to a goal again on his power-play goal with 15:16 left in the second period. The Jets forward now has eight goals in seven games. --Field Level Media

item.title: 3M to argue Australia's $1.4 billion 'forever chemicals' lawsuit legally flawed, court hears
item.description: US conglomerate 3M plans to argue a landmark case brought by Australia over contamination from the company's use of PFAS "forever chemicals" in its firefighting foam is legally flawed, a court heard on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chen
item.content:encoded: US conglomerate 3M (MMM.N) plans to argue a landmark case brought by Australia over contamination from the company's use of PFAS "forever chemicals" in its firefighting foam is legally flawed, a court heard on Friday. [USN:L1N425013 TEXT:"The claim"] against the Minnesota-based chemicals maker and its local unit is the largest ever brought by Australia, and seeks more than A$2 billion ($1.38 billion) in damages for past and future costs of contamination across 28 military bases where 3M's products were used. Australia's case is that 3M knew or ought to have known the foam it made and supplied could damage the environment and harm people, but it failed to warn the government. The foam's pollution interfered with people's ability to use and enjoy the water and land around the bases, creating what the government says amounted to a "public nuisance" under Australian law for which 3M should pay compensation. "On Australian authority, the pleaded case does not comprise public nuisance," 3M's barrister Philip Solomon said at the first case management hearing for the lawsuit on Friday. "The allegation against us alleged that we, the respondents, had the means to abate the nuisance, that we caused the nuisance, that were responsible for the particular or the special loss associated with the nuisance, and that in a broad sense, we had the ability to control the discharge of the nuisance," he added. "We will in a number of pages set out why public nuisance as pleaded is not available." In its defence, expected to be filed on December 11, 3M also plans to question whether another part of Australia's case — that the company breached consumer protection laws by making misleading claims about the foam's features and safety — was time-barred because the alleged conduct occurred decades ago, Solomon said. PFAS are a group of manufactured chemicals that are widely used in products resistant to heat, stains, grease and water. Research has linked exposure to PFAS to health issues including liver damage, lower birth weight and testicular cancer. 3M, which has faced thousands of lawsuits over alleged PFAS contamination, sold the firefighting foam in Australia from 1966 to 2003. Australia has spent A$1.3 billion in dealing with the impacts of the contamination on the bases, including paying A$408 million in legal settlements to affected communities. The defence department has also treated or removed more than 200,000 metric tons of contaminated soil and treated more than 13 billion litres of water. The case will return to court in December. ($1 = 1.4445 Australian dollars)

item.title: Indonesia's president ready to accept foreign assistance to combat fires, foreign minister says
item.description: Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto has agreed to accept assistance from neighbouring countries to tackle its worst forest fires in more than a decade, the country's foreign minister said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto has agreed to accept assistance from neighbouring countries to tackle its worst forest fires in more than a decade, the country's foreign minister said. Indonesia has come under heavy criticism after months of [USN:L6N4610Y7 TEXT:"fierce wildfires"] that have caused respiratory problems for hundreds of thousands of people and spread thick haze into neighbouring countries, leading to school closures in [USN:L6N4600NO TEXT:"Malaysia and East Timor"]. Last month, Malaysia offered to deploy three helicopters, an aircraft, and 52 personnel to help contain the fires, but there has been no follow-up since. Singapore, another country badly affected by the haze, has also said it is ready to step in to help contain the fires. "The President has already expressed his approval, and the matter is currently being discussed at the technical level within the BNPB," Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir said, according to a voice a recording shared by his ministry on Friday. BNPB is Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency. The new chief of the agency, appointed on Thursday, said he is [USN:L6N4610HK TEXT:"reviewing"] the types of assistance being offered and will decide which ones can be accelerated. The islands of Sumatra and Borneo, close to Singapore and Malaysia, have been the worst affected, with the fire able smoulder slowly beneath the surface of large stretches of peatland and re-emerge at any moment. Fire also spread to the national park of Mount Bromo in East Java, where four people involved in fighting fires were killed, the Forestry Ministry said in a statement on Friday. Two others are undergoing medical treatment for severe burns.

item.title: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks
item.description: Finance leaders of the G7 grouping agreed to hold tabletop exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks, Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said, as policymakers increasingly seek to coordinate responses to growing cyber security risks.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: Finance leaders of the G7 grouping agreed to hold tabletop exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks, Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said, as policymakers increasingly seek to coordinate responses to growing cyber security risks. The agreement comes after the International Monetary Fund [USN:L6N45Y0TS TEXT:"warned"] this week that confidence could be undermined by an AI-enabled cyber attack on a critical service of a financial institution. Katayama's remarks to reporters on Thursday followed a meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors of the G7 advanced economies held on the sidelines of the IMF's annual gathering in Bangkok, the Thai capital. The plan will feature simulations evolved by G7 finance authorities to test how they can respond to AI-driven cyber attacks, said a Japanese finance ministry official who attended the finance leaders' meeting. The results will test effectiveness of existing protocols and be used to revise manuals to better tackle such incidents, the official told reporters. The exercises by G7 finance ministries and central banks could include private financial institutions depending on the nature of simulations, the official added. Banking regulators globally are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, [USN:L6N45Z0FI TEXT:"Reuters reported"], with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability. Among them is the [USN:L6N4610NX TEXT:"Bank of England"], which is working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options, its deputy governor said on Thursday, adding that they can no longer assume their defences are immune to AI-enabled cyberattacks.

item.title: World Bank's Banga sets goal of quintupling critical minerals financing in five years
item.description: World Bank President Ajay Banga on Friday said the development lender has set a goal of quintupling its critical minerals business in five years, and has identified 20 countries that it can partner with on critical minerals development projects.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: World Bank President Ajay Banga on Friday said the development lender has set a goal of quintupling its critical minerals business in five years, and has identified 20 countries that it can partner with on critical minerals development projects. Banga revealed the new goal in prepared remarks to a plenary session at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. "In critical minerals, we plan to quintuple our business in five years," Banga said. "This week, we launched our first country compacts with MDB partners—to build local industries and keep more jobs and value at home." The World Bank's new Metals and Minerals implementation plan is targeting $19 billion in critical minerals financing over the fiscal 2026-2030 period, compared with $3.6 billion in the fiscal 2021-2025 period. Critical minerals development is an area where the United States, the World Bank's largest shareholder, has called for the bank to devote more financing resources. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier this week that he wanted the bank to play a bigger role in enabling critical minerals mining and processing capacity through project de-risking and finance and investment in enabling infrastructure. He said this includes deep-sea mining projects. Banga did not mention deep-sea mining, but the bank's metals plan calls for a "precautionary approach" to the nascent sector, adding that any engagement and investments must be consistent with applicable bank policies. Banga reviewed the World Bank's overall increases in financing during the 2026 fiscal year that ended on June 30, including mobilizing $112 billion in private capital, a more than threefold increase from the 2022 fiscal year, before he assumed his role. Alongside lending from the World Bank's own balance sheet, this brought the group's total financing to $230 billion for fiscal 2026, he said.

item.content:encoded: Asian stocks rebounded on Friday following heavy selling in the previous session when investors dumped tech shares as questions about cloud company CoreWeave's [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"debt pile"] fuelled worries about the financing driving the AI boom. Bond markets stabilized after yields plunged on Thursday as traders bought up Treasuries and other safe-haven sovereign debt. The dollar limped towards its first weekly loss in five weeks as lower US yields eroded the currency's appeal. Gold eased back from Thursday's high, while Brent crude drifted lower toward $105. Japan's tech-heavy Nikkei (.N225) rose 1.8%, making back some of Thursday's almost 5% tumble. South Korea's KOSPI (.KS11) climbed 2.8%, following a nearly 8% plunge. Taiwan's stock benchmark (.TWII) rose 0.7% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng (.HSI) added 1.1%. Mainland Chinese blue chips (.CSI300) edged 0.3% higher. Indonesia's equity benchmark (.JKSE) slumped 11% after MSCI said the country's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, and is [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"preparing"] to cut it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, a major setback likely to send money fleeing. The rupiah weakened about 0.8% to 95.0550 per dollar . US stock futures were lower, with tech-focused Nasdaq futures off 0.3% and S&P 500 futures down 0.1%, after the respective cash indexes notched small gains on Thursday. Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave (CRWV.O) recovered some composure on Thursday after starting the session by extending Wednesday's 15.5% slump amid reports that its bond yields had reached highs associated with distressed debt, triggering a broad, AI-centred equity selloff globally. Analysts also pointed to the pressure on memory maker shares this week after China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) reported progress on a next-generation DRAM architecture that could [USN:L4N45Z1B2 TEXT:"intensify competition"] with established manufacturers. "Global markets are getting very noisy once again after a period of low volatility: Wall Street is whipsawing, bond yields are swinging, currency markets are doing backflips, and commodity prices are running in multiple directions," Kyle Rodda, a markets analyst at Capital.com, wrote in a client note. "Global markets could potentially be in for a protracted period of this sort of volatility," with tech company earnings announcements due in the coming weeks, and markets also attempting to discern the trajectory of US and other major economies' interest rates, he said. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, along with a host of other global central bank officials, will speak at events at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok during the day. However, "given his notorious reticence and outright disdain for anything that resembles 'forward guidance', market participants will be forced to work hard to infer any insight from Warsh," Rodda said. Most Japanese government bond yields rose, retracing about half of Thursday's decline, as they took cues from a smaller bounce in Treasury yields on Thursday following the prior session's plunge. Lower US yields this week sapped demand for the dollar, with the dollar index languishing near 102 following a sharp pullback from Wednesday's 1-1/2-year high near 103. The index is down 0.2% for the week. That handed the euro some welcome respite, after it pulled itself up from as low as $1.1113 on Wednesday to sit at $1.1217 on Friday. The Trump administration is considering [USN:L1N461108 TEXT:"lifting sanctions"] on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday. item.title: Rupee to rise as offshore traders cut bearish bets, RBI clarifies hedging rules
item.description: The Indian rupee is poised to rally despite weakness across Asian peers, with offshore traders cutting bets against the Asian currency and expectations of continued central bank dollar selling lending support.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee is poised to rally despite weakness across Asian peers, with offshore traders cutting bets against the Asian currency and expectations of continued central bank dollar selling lending support. The rupee is expected to open in the 94.75 to 94.80 range, per traders, having settled at 95.0550 to the dollar on Thursday. Other Asian currencies dipped and the dollar index inched higher. There has been "a fair amount" of unwinding of long USD/INR positions this week, a currency trader at a foreign bank said. That is supporting the rupee in the non-deliverable forward market and with the Reserve Bank of India "quite determined" to push the rupee higher, there's probably more room for long dollar positions to be cut, he added. The dollar/rupee rate in the NDF market is trading at a discount to its onshore counterpart, a rare phenomenon, particularly at a time when the rupee's outlook remains challenging. NEW TRAJECTORY The rupee has charted its own course this week, buoyed by a series of measures by the RBI to curb dollar demand and support the currency. The measures included a reserve requirement on certain large foreign-exchange transactions for forward dollar purchases. However, a lack of clarity over which transactions were covered sowed confusion among bankers, triggering significant [USN:L1N46105F TEXT:"turbulence"] in India's FX forward market. Several banks held back from quoting prices to other banks, contributing to a drop in liquidity and exacerbating price moves. Seeking to address the concerns, the RBI issued [USN:L4N461165 TEXT:"clarifications"] after market hours on Thursday. A senior treasury official at a bank said while the clarifications "help a lot," a few ambiguities and doubts remained. Rupee forward premiums have surged this week amid a liquidity squeeze and banks cutting positions. The treasury official said the clarifications should help alleviate these market dislocations.

item.title: US appeals court invalidates federal $9 billion telecom subsidy fund
item.description: A U.S. federal appeals court said on Thursday the Federal Communications Commission exceeded its authority in setting up a telecoms subsidy program in the late 1990s used to widen access to communications for millions of Americans.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: A U.S. federal appeals court said on Thursday the Federal Communications Commission exceeded its authority in setting up a telecoms subsidy program in the late 1990s used to widen access to communications for millions of Americans. The FCC collects funds from telecom carriers through a private company for the so-called "Universal Service Fund" that subsidizes basic communications services for consumers in rural and low-income areas. However, the FCC lacked legal authority in 1997 to establish the company, the Universal Service Administrative Co, to collect the funds and set contribution rates, said Judge Edith Brown Clement. "Because Congress never specifically authorized the FCC to establish USAC, we hold that the agency violated the Government Corporation Control Act," she wrote for a three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. The FCC was considering all options available to it, a spokesperson said in response to Thursday's decision. "While the court takes issue today with an FCC decision made almost 30 years ago, the court’s order would not go into effect until two months from now, at the earliest," the spokesperson added in a statement. The fund draws about $9 billion a year, with the vast majority of telecoms companies passing on the cost to customers. In addition to low-income and rural areas, the fund has been used to widen services to Native American tribal lands, as well as enabling schools, libraries and rural health care facilities to obtain essential communications services. In June 2025, the U.S. Supreme Court endorsed the way the FCC funds the multi-billion dollar program. The ruling overturned an earlier Fifth Circuit decision that the FCC's funding mechanism employing mandatory contributions from telecoms companies had effectively levied a "misbegotten tax" on consumers. U.S. telecom providers get billions of dollars in payments from the Universal Service Fund and millions of consumers rely on such government-subsidized services for internet access or phone service. In 2024, the FCC program benefited 7.5 million low-income households and gave telecom companies $4.2 billion to provide high-speed internet service in hard-to-serve rural areas. It also gave 118,000 schools and libraries $7 billion over a three-year period for internet service for 54 million students. The FCC, overseen by Congress, was set up as an independent federal agency in 1934.

item.title: Copp, Red Wings nab home victory to extend Flyers' winless streak

item.content:encoded: Andrew Copp scored the go-ahead goal with 4:38 remaining in the third period, fueling the host Detroit Red Wings to a 2-1 victory over the winless Philadelphia Flyers on Thursday. Copp scored his first goal of the season after crashing the crease to beat Philadelphia defenseman David Jiricek to a loose puck. Defenseman Anton Johansson scored his first career NHL goal and Daniil Tarasov made 17 saves for the Red Wings, who snapped a three-game winless skid (0-1-2). Matvei Michkov scored his team-leading third goal of the season and Joseph Woll turned aside 24 shots for the Flyers, who extended their franchise-record winless streak to start a season to nine games (0-6-3). They have mustered just 11 goals during that stretch and are one of two teams (the Los Angeles Kings) yet to win a game this season. Philadelphia failed on both of its attempts on the power play. Detroit, in turn, went 0-for-4 with the man advantage. Defenseman Travis Sanheim unleashed a shot from the left circle that was batted home by Michkov, who was stationed at the side of the net. The goal opened the scoring with 2:28 remaining in the first period. Detroit nearly answered late in the period, however former captain Dylan Larkin's shot caromed off the post. The Red Wings forged a 1-1 tie at 4:31 of the second period after Philadelphia's Owen Tippett committed a turnover. A 2-on-1 rush developed, and Larkin feathered a pass that was one-timed home by Johansson. Detroit was unable to convert a power play that bridged the second and third periods. The Red Wings were able to have the man advantage after Philadelphia's Tyson Foerster inexplicably tripped Alex DeBrincat while the latter was without a stick in his hand. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brady Tkachuk caps 2nd straight hat trick in OT as Panthers top Canucks
item.description: Brady Tkachuk scored twice in the final nine minutes of regulation, then completed his second straight natural hat trick 2:23 into overtime, leading the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 come-from-behind victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday in Sunrise, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brady Tkachuk scored twice in the final nine minutes of regulation, then completed his second straight natural hat trick 2:23 into overtime, leading the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 come-from-behind victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday in Sunrise, Fla. Tkachuk is the first player since the Toronto Maple Leafs' Auston Matthews in February 2024 to record a hat trick in back-to-back games. He is the third Panther with a hat trick in consecutive games (Noel Acciari and Pavel Bure) and the second to complete a hat trick in overtime (Aleksander Barkov). Panthers goalie Akira Schmid, making his third consecutive appearance and second straight start while Jacob Markstrom remains day-to-day with an undisclosed injury, stopped 15 shots. Seth Jones logged two assists as the Panthers won two straight games for the first time this season. Liam Ohgren and Elias Pettersson scored for Vancouver, which took its sixth loss in a row (0-5-1). Merilainen, who allowed six goals in his previous two outings, was stout throughout the night, finishing with 36 saves as the Canucks dropped to 0-4-1 on a six-game road trip. Down 2-0, Florida began its comeback. Tkachuk, who scored his first three goals with his new team during the Panthers' 7-3 victory at Columbus on Tuesday, sent a one-time wrister past Vancouver goaltender Leevi Merilainen, with 8:49 remaining in the third period. An Aaron Ekblad drop pass set up the tally. With 13 seconds to go in regulation and Schmid pulled for an extra skater, Tkachuk got enough on a bouncing puck to score through traffic. "The Panthers applied pressure from the start of overtime, and Tkachuk ended the game by beating Merilainen from point-blank range. Moments after killing off a Florida power play, the Canucks opened the scoring 7:23 into the first period on their first shot on goal. The Panthers struggled to clear their zone, and the puck found the stick of Vancouver's Linus Karlsson, who sent it into the slot for Ohgren to one-time past Schmid. The Canucks, outshot 15-7 through the first 20 minutes, made it 2-0 with 2:54 left in the opening period. Off a side-board scrum for the puck, it got out to Vancouver's Filip Chytil, who sent a back-handed pass into the slot for a wide-open Pettersson to bury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Victor Hedman's OT winner gives Lightning 4th straight home win
item.description: Tampa Bay's Victor Hedman drove through the slot and scored at 2:07 of overtime as the Lightning beat the Seattle Kraken 4-3 on Thursday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tampa Bay's Victor Hedman drove through the slot and scored at 2:07 of overtime as the Lightning beat the Seattle Kraken 4-3 on Thursday night. The captain appeared to lose control of the puck while splitting the defense, but he lunged forward and swatted it past Grubauer for his first goal of the season. The Lightning improved to 4-0-0 at home this season. Brandon Hagel potted two goals and Ilya Mikheyev notched his 100th career tally. Goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy made 24 saves. All-time, the Lightning are 9-0-2 against the Kraken, while Vasilevskiy improved to 8-0-1 against them. Dominic James (hand) made his season debut after breaking his hand in September and recorded an assist. Seattle's Matty Beniers registered his 200th career point with a goal, and Ryan Winterton and Jared McCann hit the net. Seattle goaltender Philipp Grubauer stopped 31 shots as the club slipped to 3-0-1 on its five-game road trip. Vasilevskiy left the puck behind the net for Emil Lilleberg, but Frederick Gaudreau pressured the defenseman and sent the puck in front to Winterton, who backhanded it home for his second goal of the season at 5:43. After taking a pass from Brayden Point, Hagel skated through the right circle and fired a shot into Grubauer's chest, then knocked in his own rebound to tie the game at 16:53. Hagel ripped a nasty snipe past Grubauer at 3:38 in the second for his sixth goal, and the Lightning's penalty-kill units killed off Seattle's consecutive power plays. Vasilevskiy made the one-goal lead stand up by denying Shane Wright on a point-blank chance with 43 seconds left. However, James committed an interference penalty inside the first three minutes of the third. McCann scored for the third time this season when he finished a slick feed from Jordan Eberle just seven seconds into the power play at 2:54. The home side forced a turnover behind Grubauer midway through the third, and Mikheyev batted in the puck to reach the century mark for the go-ahead goal. Beniers knotted it 3-all when he tipped in his second goal over Vasilevskiy at 15:41 on a long shot by Vince Dunn. --Field Level Media

item.title: Investors see outflow and FX risks as MSCI moves to downgrade Indonesia
item.description: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, MSCI said, and the index provider proposed to cut it from a suite of products tracked by global investors.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"MSCI said"], and the index provider proposed to cut it from a suite of products tracked by global investors. The move is a major setback likely to send money fleeing. Here is what market participants are saying: ANGUS MACKINTOSH, ASEAN SPECIALIST, ALETHIA CAPITAL, SINGAPORE: "The move seems heavy-handed given the moves that Indonesia has made to address issues around market visibility and free float. The problem for Indonesia is a lack of evidence of implementation and a failure to sanction those obviously involved in stock manipulation. The only way for Indonesia to remedy this situation would be to impose severe sanctions and fines on those involved in concerted share manipulation. "This move does not reflect the health of the vast majority of listed companies or indeed the Indonesian economy, and grouping Indonesia with Lebanon, Palestine, and Argentina does not make sense." RADHIKA RAO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, DBS BANK, SINGAPORE: "This potential development could prove more unfavourable than a tier reclassification, as passive investors bound by mandate may also reduce exposure. Any ensuing risk-off move in the currency would likely prompt greater central bank vigilance and intervention." GARY TAN, PORTFOLIO MANAGER, ALLSPRING GLOBAL INVESTMENTS, SINGAPORE: "The consultation is a surprise given the steps Indonesia has already taken to improve market accessibility, including removing the minimum share price limit. The prospect of standalone status could encourage index-linked investors to further de-risk, but for Indonesia in our view the bigger concern is less the direct impact on equities and more the potential pressure on the currency from foreign outflows." IRMAN FAIZ, ECONOMIST, BANK DANAMON INDONESIA: "MSCI's unusually strong assessment increases the incentive for institutional investors to reduce exposure ahead of the final decision, potentially extending equity volatility and weakening foreign risk appetite. "The larger risk is structural from a reduced institutional participation, thinner liquidity, to higher equity financing costs. Large-cap banks are particularly exposed, while spillovers into sovereign bonds would depend on broader investor risk appetite rather than automatic index-related selling." JAYDEN VANTARAKIS, HEAD OF ASEAN EQUITY RESEARCH, MACQUARIE CAPITAL, SINGAPORE: "The working assumption for most equity investors we’d spoken with recently had been that steps taken on free-floats and shareholder concentration disclosure would be sufficient to avert a downgrade." "The extension of the review from November 2026 to June 2027 also prolongs the period of uncertainty for investors."

item.title: Owen Power completes Sabres' comeback with OT winner vs. Leafs
item.description: Owen Power scored in overtime as the visiting Buffalo Sabres came from behind to top the Toronto Maple Leafs 5-4 on Thursday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Owen Power scored in overtime as the visiting Buffalo Sabres came from behind to top the Toronto Maple Leafs 5-4 on Thursday night. Power nabbed his second overtime winner of the season, receiving a pass from Jack Quinn and launching it past goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky blocker side. Quinn recorded four points and a Gordie Howe hat trick for the Sabres after a second-period tussle with Troy Stecher. Mattias Samuelsson, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson had multi-point games for Buffalo, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 26 saves in his third win of the season. Kirill Marchenko scored a hat trick for Toronto. John Tavares had two assists but went to the dressing room in the third period after a collision with Josh Norris. The Sabres have won four of their last five against Toronto. Buffalo trailed 4-2 after two periods, but about halfway through the third Dennis Gilbert brought his team within one off a low shot from the point. It was the fourth goal of the journeyman defenseman's career and his first since 2023. Samuelsson tied the game two minutes later off a give-and-go with Tage Thompson. Toronto was outshot 11-4 in the third. Auston Matthews plucked Samuelsson's clearing attempt out of the air and left the puck for Jack Roslovic, who played it back to the captain making a beeline towards the net. Matthews flipped the puck past a helpless Luukkonen to open the scoring in the early going, extending his points streak to six games. Quinn tied it up just over a minute later, Benson snatching the puck off Nick Blankenburg and slipping the puck to Quinn in the slot. Marchenko put the home team back in the lead with a highlight-reel goal on the power play, pulling the puck through his legs and lifting it over Luukkonen in tight. Quinn ripped in his second of the game early in the middle frame, dragging the puck around the stick of Jake McCabe to wrist it past Bobrovsky from the high slot. Sitting on a hat trick, Quinn proceeded to strike iron twice in the second period. Marchenko flicked in his second of the game from the edge of the faceoff circle to put the Maple Leafs up 3-2. Colton Sissons helped him to a hat trick five minutes later with a slick feed from behind the goal line, Marchenko firing it in off a one-timer from close range. --Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Summer Zhen, Anirban Sen
item.content:encoded: Global hedge funds suffered steep losses this week, according to a Goldman Sachs prime brokerage note, battered by the violent unwind of a swathe of AI bets, with Asia-focused funds hit the hardest. Investors are increasingly [USN:L1N45Z05C TEXT:"questioning"] whether massive AI spending can [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"pay off"] anytime soon as elevated inflation keeps borrowing costs high. Global fundamental long-short funds, or stock pickers, lost money every single day this week, Goldman Sachs said, with losses for the week to October 15 coming to 2.9%. For the year to date, though, they have gains of 14.3%. On Wednesday, hedge funds across strategies retreated sharply, with stock pickers globally losing 0.9%. Among them, Asia-focused managers were down 2.6%, while tech-focused funds were off 2.0%. Global systematic long-short managers and multi-strategy funds also declined roughly 1%. Hotter-than-expected US inflation data this week that increased expectations of further rate hikes also fuelled the selloff in semiconductor and AI supply chain stocks. "From COVID through end-2025, all three broad strategies never fell more than 80bps on the same day," Goldman Sachs said, adding that this has now occurred three times this year, on February 4, July 28 and October 15. Semiconductor-heavy markets bore the brunt of the selloff. South Korea's benchmark KOSPI (.KS11) tumbled 8% to close at a six-month low on Thursday, while Taiwan stocks also lost more than 3%. Asia-focused stock pickers have lost 6.8% for the first half of this month and have erased more than half of the gains from their late-June peak, when they were up more than 40% for the year, according to Goldman Sachs.

item.title: Shane Pinto lifts Senators past Islanders in shootout
item.description: Shane Pinto scored the only goal in the shootout Thursday night for the host Ottawa Senators, who outlasted the New York Islanders 2-1.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Shane Pinto scored the only goal in the shootout Thursday night for the host Ottawa Senators, who outlasted the New York Islanders 2-1. Pinto, the Senators' third skater in the shootout, shuffled the puck as he approached Islanders goalie Semyon Varlamov before sending a shot beyond Varlamov's glove. Ottawa goalie Linus Ullmark then stopped New York's Simon Holmstrom to seal the win. Ridly Greig scored in the second for the Senators, who have won six of their first eight games (6-2-0). Ullmark made 20 saves in regulation and overtime. Matias Maccelli scored for the second straight game for the Islanders, who have alternated wins and losses in their first seven contests (3-3-1). Varlamov, seeking his first win since Nov. 14, 2024, made 18 saves. The 38-year-old missed last season while recovering from double partial knee replacements. The Senators had two potential first-period goals overturned on video review before Maccelli put New York ahead with an unassisted tally with 11.2 seconds remaining. Warren Foegele appeared to give Ottawa the lead 4:50 into the game, but the puck slid along the goal line without fully crossing it. The Islanders' challenge was successful with 8:06 left, when Stephen Halliday's goal was disallowed after a review showed the Senators were offside. Maccelli finally broke the scoreless tie when he stole the puck from Pinto deep in the Ottawa zone, took a couple strides and fired a shot over Ullmark's glove as Islanders center Bo Horvat and Senators defenseman Thomas Chabot skated into the shooting lane. Greig tied the score with 4:17 left in the second. Artem Zub sent a clearing pass from Ottawa's goal line through the neutral zone to Foegele, who threaded a backhanded feed past a sliding Kyle Palmieri. Greig collected the puck and flicked a shot over Varlamov's blocker. Both teams picked up penalties in overtime, but the Islanders killed off Adam Pelech's hooking call at the 1:52 mark and the Senators burned the final 59 seconds after Dylan Cozens was whistled for tripping. --Field Level Media

item.title: Luke Hughes nets 2 goals in Devils' 7-1 domination of Rangers
item.description: Luke Hughes led the way with two of the New Jersey Devils' four second-period goals to help bury their rival New York Rangers 7-1 in Newark, N.J. on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Luke Hughes led the way with two of the New Jersey Devils' four second-period goals to help bury their rival New York Rangers 7-1 in Newark, N.J. on Thursday. Nico Daws stopped 18 shots in the victory, while Nico Hischier, Arseny Gritsyuk, Evan Rodrigues, Cody Glass, and Stefan Noesen all joined Hughes on the scoresheet. Timo Meier, Dougie Hamilton, Brett Pesce, Dawson Mercer, and Amadeus Lombardi all picked up a pair of assists each. Pavel Dorofeyev scored the Rangers' lone goal as they allowed more than three goals for the first time this season. Rodrigues took advantage of a tough giveaway and ripped it past Dylan Garand with 30 seconds remaining in the first period to give the Devils the lead. Hughes fired a point shot that bounced off a defender and snuck through the legs of Garand to double the Devils' advantage just 18 seconds into the middle frame. Hischier then made it 3-0 barely over four minutes into the second. After the Devils captain fired his shot wide on an odd-man rush, he stuck around and poked a rebound past the pad of an outstretched Garand. The Devils kept rolling just 31 seconds later as Gritsyuk made up for a missed breakaway by pouncing on a rebound and lighting the lamp, marking the end of Garand's night after he allowed four goals on 13 shots. Spencer Martin gave up three goals on 18 shots in relief. The youngest Hughes brother showcased his impressive skillset as he walked the blueline and cut in toward the net. He sent a shot off the far post and into the back of the net for his second goal of the night with 3:26 left in the second. Noesen buried his first goal of the season to make it 6-0 with just over seven minutes gone in the third period. Dorofeyev spoiled Daws' shutout bid with a power-play marker just over a minute later. Glass got in on the action to make it 7-1 with just over five minutes left in the contest. --Field Level Media

item.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia says she did not pass bar exam
item.description: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said on Thursday she did not pass the bar exam after facing scrutiny about her legal career before becoming the top spokeswoman for US President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: New White House press secretary [USN:L6N4601D0 TEXT:"Katie Zacharia"] said on Thursday she did not pass the bar exam after facing scrutiny about her legal career before becoming the top spokeswoman for US President Donald Trump . Zacharia, who joined the White House on Monday, has previously said she practiced law before entering politics and Trump had described her as an attorney. "You did not pass the bar exam, correct?" she was asked in an interview on Fox News' "Hannity" show late on Thursday. "Correct," she said in response to the host, Sean Hannity. "I did not," she said when Hannity asked if she ever took the bar exam a second time. Zacharia earned her law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, according to the university. Nearly all licensed US lawyers first obtain a law degree, but law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar. On Tuesday during her first briefing, she took questions from just three reporters before ending the event in under 15 minutes. Her performance was criticized by some media commentators and political analysts, though Trump told reporters, "I thought she was very good." When asked about her performance by Hannity, she said: "What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference, Sean, with very little prep time."

item.title: MSCI freezes certain Turkey index changes, warns of potential market downgrade
item.description: MSCI on Thursday froze certain changes to its Turkey equity indexes, saying it needed more time to assess market reforms and warning of a potential downgrade if sufficient progress was not made by mid-2027.
item.dc:creator: Mrinmay Dey, Rodrigo Campos
item.content:encoded: MSCI (MSCI.N) on Thursday froze certain changes to its Turkey equity indexes, saying it needed more time to assess market reforms and warning of a potential downgrade if sufficient progress was not made by mid-2027. Turkey's equity market has [USN:L8N45A0T5 TEXT:"faced investor scrutiny"] over free-float calculations and suspected coordinated trading in some stocks. MSCI's decision leaves Turkey's emerging-market status unchanged, but a future downgrade to frontier-market status could trigger selling by funds that track the MSCI Emerging Markets Index. The freeze took effect immediately and will remain in place until further notice, affecting changes stemming from index reviews and corporate events involving Turkish securities. MSCI said the decision followed concerns raised during its 2026 Market Classification Review over "possible coordinated trading through fund holdings closely affiliated with certain smaller listed companies." Such activity could undermine the reliability of free-float estimates and broader market integrity, the index provider said. "Institutional investors will need to see credible and sustained enforcement against coordinated trading, and disclosure standards that enable independent verification of the free float of Turkish securities," MSCI said. Turkey has a relatively small pool of stocks that meet the size and liquidity requirements of global institutional investors, concentrating capital in a handful of names and increasing scrutiny of free-float calculations and trading activity. The benchmark BIST 100 (.XU100) is on track for a fifth straight weekly decline and is down more than 20% from its record closing high in May. Under the freeze, MSCI will not increase foreign inclusion factors or the number of shares used in its indexes, add securities to the MSCI Turkey Investable Market Index, or make upward migrations across size-segment indexes. MSCI said that if sufficient progress was not evident by June 2027, it could take further steps, including consulting on a potential downgrade of Turkey from emerging-market to frontier- or standalone-market status. It will continue seeking feedback from market participants and monitoring the effectiveness of regulatory and enforcement measures. S&P Dow Jones Indices (SPGI.N) also warned in July that Turkey [USN:FWN4390QT TEXT:"risked a downgrade"] to frontier-market status from emerging-market status over market transparency and other concerns.

item.title: Trump diz que está conversando com Rússia e China sobre desnuclearização
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que Washington mantém negociações com Moscou e Pequim com o objetivo de desnuclearizar os países com os maiores arsenais de armas nucleares.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que Washington mantém negociações com Moscou e Pequim com o objetivo de desnuclearizar os países com os maiores arsenais de armas nucleares. A Rússia possui o maior número de ogivas nucleares armazenadas, seguida pelos Estados Unidos e pela China, de acordo com o Instituto Internacional de Pesquisa para a Paz de Estocolmo. Os EUA superam a Rússia no número de ogivas implantadas. Durante uma entrevista à Newsmax, Trump disse esperar que a China “alcance” os EUA nos próximos cinco anos. “Tudo isso é uma pena, porque eu adoraria promover a desnuclearização, se possível, mas, na verdade, estamos conversando com a Rússia sobre isso e também com a China sobre a desnuclearização”, disse Trump ao veículo. A Newsmax informou que Trump havia conversado com o presidente chinês Xi Jinping sobre a desnuclearização. Os comentários de Trump ocorrem meses após o vencimento do Tratado de Redução de Armas Estratégicas, no início deste ano. O novo Tratado Start, assinado em 2010, permitia uma única prorrogação, que foi acordada pelo ex-presidente Joe Biden e pelo presidente russo Vladimir Putin por cinco anos. Qualquer nova prorrogação exige uma decisão executiva para estender voluntariamente os limites do tratado.
