Lula will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, in an election runoff on Oct. 25, after the senator [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"surprisingly led"] him in the first round Opposition lawmakers have proposed including a reduction in the minimum age of criminal responsibility in a government-backed bill aimed at strengthening the powers of the federal government in public safety The bill was set to be voted on Thursday in the Senate, but the vote was postponed amid the debate over whether to include changes in the criminal responsibility age Lula said that reducing the age of criminal responsibility should not be discussed in that bill, arguing that the proposal before Congress focuses on a different issue Opposition lawmakers, including Bolsonaro, supported lowering the minimum age of criminal responsibility to 16 years in general, and to 14 for violent crimes

item.title: Jenna Ortega plays an artificial friend in need in 'Klara and the Sun'
item.description: In Taika Waititi's "Klara and the Sun", which stars Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams, a robot delivers lessons on humanity.
item.dc:creator: Hanna Rantala
item.content:encoded: In Taika Waititi's "Klara and the Sun", which stars Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams, a robot delivers lessons on humanity. The dystopian drama is based on Nobel Prize-winning author Kazuo Ishiguro's 2021 bestseller of the same name and set in a technologically advanced future, following what one character describes as a third world war triggered by the abuse of the internet. Ortega plays Klara, an outdated model of an Artificial Friend, an android companion whose sell-by date is fast approaching when, to her relief, teenager Josie (Mia Tharia) and her mother (Adams) buy her. Programmed to prevent loneliness, Klara is full of quirks and hopes and believes in the healing power of the sun. Her traits come in handy in a household marked by grief and mystery. "It felt like a very timely story," said Ortega at the movie's world premiere at the London Film Festival on Thursday. "To see it put in a futuristic world and see that we still struggle with the same things and the answer's kind of always in one another and listening to one another, I thought it was a really nuanced, thoughtful way of putting it." Waititi, who directed, co-wrote and produced the movie, was struck by Ishiguro's allegorical interplay between humans, artificial intelligence and nature. "She's a machine who comes into the world of a broken family and somehow teaches them the importance of being human," Waititi said. "It's vital right now because we're now in a moment where we're maybe on the cusp of losing control of our relationship with technology," said Waititi, adding that he also wanted the film to "remind people to put the devices down, not because there's a threat or anything, but just put the thing down because it's a distraction, and just be with the people you're with." While Waititi injected some of his signature humour into the movie, he said he wanted to "keep the profound feeling and the drama from the book". "There's some funny bits there, but it's probably my most dramatic film," Waititi said. "Klara and the Sun", which also stars Natasha Lyonne, Steve Buscemi, Aran Murphy and Rachel House, will go on release globally from October 21.

item.title: Australia names offshore site for Inpex-led Bonaparte carbon storage project
item.description: Australia on Friday designated the West Peron undersea rock formation, off the country's north coast, as a storage site for the 8 million metric ton-per-year Bonaparte carbon capture and storage project proposed by Japan's Inpex .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia on Friday designated the West Peron undersea rock formation, off the country's north coast, as a storage site for the 8 million metric ton-per-year Bonaparte carbon capture and storage project proposed by Japan's Inpex (1605.T) . The Bonaparte project is initially expected to receive carbon dioxide from Inpex's Ichthys liquefied natural gas (LNG) project before eventually expanding storage services to multiple industrial facilities. Inpex proposes to permanently store up to 443 million tons of carbon dioxide deep underground in the West Peron formation over a period of up to 35 years. The formation is a layer of porous rock located deep beneath the seabed. Australia Resources Minister Madeleine King said the decision demonstrated the government's support for technologies aimed at reducing emissions from industries where cutting greenhouse gas emissions remains difficult. "Carbon capture and storage will play an important role in reducing emissions from hard-to-abate industries, supporting Australia's transition to net zero," King said. Australia has a legislated target to reach net zero emissions by 2050.

item.title: Euro gets much-needed reprieve as AI wobbles rock the dollar
item.description: The dollar headed for its first weekly fall in five weeks on Friday, lifting the euro from a 17-month low as wobbles in AI investment and drop in US yields put the brakes on recent gains.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The dollar headed for its first weekly fall in five weeks on Friday, lifting the euro from a 17-month low as wobbles in AI investment and drop in US yields put the brakes on recent gains. AI stocks have [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"cratered"] this week and the [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"stress spread"] to parts of the credit market as investors who have crowded in to bets all along the AI supply chain [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"worry"] that data centre operators might not manage to be profitable in time to pay their debts. The result, so far, has been a flight to [USN:L4N46108S TEXT:"Treasuries"], where the US 10-year yield is set for its largest weekly fall in more than a year, and to sell a dollar which has been propelled, in part, thanks to the AI boom boosting the economy. Moves in the Asia morning were slight, leaving the dollar down 0.2% this week at 158.13 yen and shedding about 0.1% to $1.1210 per euro . The reversal has come not a moment too soon for the common currency, which over the previous five weeks had dropped more than 3% on the dollar on jitters about France's growing debt pile and a winter energy squeeze. With the market positioned long in dollars, more AI wobbles could unwind that and push the dollar down further. "The reaction function of the dollar to a serious repricing of the AI capex boom should be unambiguously dollar bearish," said Spectra Markets president Brent Donnelly. "If the market is pricing rising odds of peak AI capex, the USD is a sell. The entire US economy is a one-legged stool balanced on the AI trade." The dollar index , which measures the US currency against six major peers, was at 102.07, set for a 0.14% drop in the week. Sterling was steady at $1.3270 for a weekly rise of 0.3%, helped by data showing Britain's economy unexpectedly grew 0.1% in August. The New Zealand dollar looked likely to scratch out a weekly gain of 0.1% at $0.5621. The Australian dollar was flat at $0.6921 and an outlier in heading for a fall of 0.8% on the dollar this week, after a surprisingly soft jobs report on Thursday had markets paring back expectations for another rise in interest rates. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in Bangkok on Friday at 0330 GMT (11:30 p.m. ET Thursday) at the International Monetary Fund's annual meeting, a final chance to shape market expectations for the Fed's decision in less than two weeks. "Given Warsh’s distaste for forward guidance, he might subtly signal his preference for the October rate outcome," said Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia. "Any hints from Warsh can influence the October Fed pricing and the USD sharply today." Traders are pricing in a 72% chance of the Fed standing pat later this month, up from 53% a month earlier, the CME FedWatch tool showed. The expected likelihood of a hike rose sharply after a hotter-than-expected CPI report this week, but bets eased after Fed officials said the central bank could wait for more clarity before the meeting.

item.title: Lógico que estou preocupado com aumento da dívida pública, diz Lula
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reconheceu nesta quinta-feira que tem preocupação com o aumento da dívida pública e defendeu o crescimento econômico como forma de resolver o problema fiscal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reconheceu nesta quinta-feira que tem preocupação com o aumento da dívida pública e defendeu o crescimento econômico como forma de resolver o problema fiscal. O presidente afirmou ainda, em entrevista à TV Globo, que sabe que se as contas públicas saírem do controle, os mais pobres sofrerão as consequências com mais intensidade. "Você acha que eu não estou preocupado? É lógico que eu estou preocupado. Eu criei uma família com 5 filhos, eu sei o que é dívida", disse Lula, na entrevista. "Eu trato com muito respeito essa questão da dívida, eu não quero que a dívida cresça", acrescentou. No final de agosto, em entrevista ao Jornal Nacional, Lula havia afirmado que a [USN:L1N44P00V TEXT:"dívida"] pública não era motivo de preocupação e que o país deve registrar superávit fiscal neste ano. A condução da situação fiscal do país é um dos pontos levantados por críticos ao presidente, que tenta a reeleição em disputa com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). Os dois se enfrentam nas urnas no dia 25 deste mês, quando ocorrem as votações do segundo turno. Dado divulgado pelo Banco Central no fim de setembro aponta que a [USN:L1N45M0F3 TEXT:"dívida"] bruta do Brasil subiu a 82,9% do PIB em agosto.

item.title: South Africa's Rabada primed to bring the heat in second test, Wade warns Australia
item.description: Matthew Wade has warned Australia to expect a more dangerous South African attack with pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada poised to return for the second test in Gqeberha and make an impact with his trademark aggression.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Matthew Wade has warned Australia to expect a more dangerous South African attack with pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada poised to return for the second test in Gqeberha and make an impact with his trademark aggression. Rabada missed Australia’s 214-run victory in Durban with a hamstring injury but is in contention for Sunday’s match at St George’s Park, where reigning World Test champions South Africa will look to level the three-test series. “The thing that stands out with him is his competitiveness,” Wade, Australia's assistant coach, told reporters. “He takes it to the opposition, he'll be in our face, he'll keep coming for the whole test match, so we really know that.” Wade, who worked with Rabada in the Indian Premier League, said the bowler's ability to sustain pressure would give the hosts greater versatility after they struggled to contain Australia in the series-opener. "They went with two spinners last time but ... him and (Anrich) Nortje can basically take one quick spot and (do) short spells and really attack as hard if they want to.” Wade was downbeat about Cameron Green's chances of returning for Australia for the second test, having missed Durban with an abdominal strain. The all-rounder had returned to batting in the nets but was more likely for the series finale in Cape Town, he said. That may mean another chance for Nic Maddinson, who was a surprise pick to open the batting with Travis Head in Durban, with Matt Renshaw moving down the order to score 190 and 82 in a match-winning performance at number five. Despite the result, former Australia captain [USN:L6N46104A TEXT:"Steve Waugh"] called for the team's selectors to stop changing the batting order, and let players settle in fixed roles. Wade said the players were happy to be flexible. "If the conditions tell us it's time to change the batting order, we'll make that change," he said. "We've seen over the last little bit that we've been able to adapt really quickly and more importantly the players take it on so easily - and credit to them."

item.title: Trump says he is talking to Russia and China about denuclearization
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday Washington is holding talks with Moscow and Beijing aimed at denuclearizing the countries with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday Washington is holding talks with Moscow and Beijing aimed at denuclearizing the countries with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons. Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The US outpaces Russia on its number of deployed warheads. During an interview with Newsmax, Trump said he expects China to "catch up" with the US within the next five years. "The whole thing is a shame, because I'd love to denuclearize if possible, but we're actually talking to Russia about that, and we're talking to China about that denuclearization," Trump told the outlet. Newsmax reported that Trump had spoken with Chinese President Xi Jinping about denuclearization. Trump's comments come months after the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty [USN:FWN3Z10T1 TEXT:"expired"] earlier this year. The New START treaty signed in 2010 allowed one single extension, which was agreed by former President Joe Biden and Russian President Vladimir Putin for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty.

item.title: Oil edges down as investors weigh possible US sanctions on 'shadow fleet'
item.description: Oil prices edged down on Friday morning as investors weighed Middle East risks and possible US steps to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers.
item.dc:creator: Sam Li, Lewis Jackson
item.content:encoded: Oil prices edged down on Friday morning as investors weighed Middle East risks and possible US steps to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers. Brent crude futures fell 41 cents, or 0.39%, to $105.51 a barrel by 0012 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures CLc1 were down 54 cents, or 0.55%, to $97.43. WTI settled up more than 3% on Thursday after a large US crude stock [USN:L6N46115T TEXT:"draw"] helped support prices, while Brent crude was little changed. The International Energy Agency [USN:L1N4610MY TEXT:"agreed"] on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market and any oil remaining from a record release of emergency reserves pledged in March to boost supply and cool soaring prices. During the previous trading session, oil prices rose overnight in a sign that "investors were dissatisfied with these measures," Haitong Futures in a note on Friday. "What would really cool the oil market is an easing of tensions in the Middle East." The Trump administration is considering [USN:L1N461108 TEXT:"lifting"] sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday. The discussions come days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with a torrent of criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans in the US Senate. Meanwhile, escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis and renewed attacks on ships in the region supported prices. [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"Attacks"] around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. The Houthis [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"fired"] missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict.

item.title: China says Israel should stop its 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements
item.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse its "forced establishment" of West Bank settlements, China's foreign ministry said in a statement on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse its "forced establishment" of West Bank settlements, China's foreign ministry said in a statement on Friday. China has consistently held that the Palestinian question is the greatest historical injustice of this century, Wang told Herzog during a meeting in Azerbaijan, the ministry added. Wang said that promoting peace and reconciliation in the region is the "cornerstone" of China's Middle East policy China believes that the "two-state solution" is the right path to a resolution and the immediate priority is to fully open access to the Gaza Strip so a humanitarian "catastrophe" is not allowed to spread, Wang added At the same time, Israel should stop and reverse its forced establishment of settlements in the West Bank, he said China is willing to work with the international community to push all parties to return to dialogue and consultation as soon as possible and seek a political settlement of the conflict, Wang added China has long been a supporter of the Palestinian cause and Beijing also has close ties with Israel's main regional foe, Iran

item.title: Lula declara ser favorável à redução da maioridade penal em crimes hediondos para 16 anos
item.description: O presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou nesta quinta-feira que é favorável à redução da maioridade penal em casos de crimes hediondos de 18 para 16 anos, em uma mudança nas posições tradicionalmente defendidas pelo seu partido.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou nesta quinta-feira que é favorável à redução da maioridade penal em casos de crimes hediondos de 18 para 16 anos, em uma mudança nas posições tradicionalmente defendidas pelo seu partido. "Meu pensamento, enquanto cidadão brasileiro: todo e qualquer crime hediondo eu sou favorável a diminuir a maioridade", disse Lula em entrevista à TV Globo. Nesta quinta, o senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE), um dos coordenadores da campanha de Lula, propôs uma emenda à Proposta de Emenda Constitucional (PEC) da Segurança Pública, proposta pelo governo, com a redução da maioridade penal para 16 anos no caso de crimes hediondos, em um movimento articulado com o presidente. A proposta de Camilo foi feita para tentar se contrapor a uma outra emenda, do senador Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), coordenador da campanha do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), adversário de Lula na disputa presidencial, que reduz a maioridade para 16 anos na maior parte dos crimes e para 14 anos nos crimes hediondos. A PEC, que teve sua aprovação na Comissão de Constituição e Justiça concluída na quarta-feira, chegou a entrar na pauta do plenário nesta quinta, mas foi retirada por decisão do presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), por não haver acordo, já que as emendas foram apresentadas de última hora. Na entrevista, Lula ponderou que, apesar de defender a proposta de Camilo, a sua avaliação é que a PEC da Segurança não era o instrumento adequado, já que não tratava desse tema especificamente. "Eu sou favorável a reduzir para 16, mas não discutindo nesta PEC", afirmou. A proposta enfrenta restrições dentro do próprio PT, que sempre foi contrário à redução em qualquer situação. Lula foi perguntado ainda por que seu governo mantém níveis de aprovação inferiores a 50% da população, e o porquê do resultado adverso no primeiro turno, quando perdeu de Flávio Bolsonaro por quase 2 pontos percentuais. O presidente assumiu a responsabilidade. "Acho que tudo é responsabilidade minha. Veja, eu sou o governo. Se eu não consegui ser compreendido sobre o governo que fiz, não posso jogar a culpa em ninguém, a culpa é minha", afirmou. O presidente revelou, ainda, que não sabia que o Bolsa Família ainda não tinha sido reajustado em seu governo - o primeiro reajuste foi anunciado alguns dias antes do primeiro turno e entra em vigor na semana que vem. A medida foi apontada como eleitoreira por seus adversários. "Eu não sabia. É impensável, mas aconteceu", afirmou. "É inexplicável que em um governo do Lula não se pense em reajustar o Bolsa Família."

item.title: North Korea missile chief questions South Korea hypersonic glide vehicle test
item.description: North Korea's missile chief said South Korea's newly tested hypersonic glide vehicle may not have achieved hypersonic flight as claimed, state media KCNA reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea's missile chief said South Korea's newly tested hypersonic glide vehicle may not have achieved hypersonic flight as claimed, state media KCNA reported on Thursday. Jang Chang Ha, head of North Korea's Missile Administration, said photographs released by South Korea after its October 8 test showed no visible signs associated with hypersonic flight. "It is hard to believe that it underwent hypersonic flight circumstances characterised by extremely high temperatures as its outside appearance is so clean with its coating paint remaining intact, not stained with any soot," said Jang. Responding to the North Korean remarks, South Korea's Defence Ministry said in a statement that the missile was designed with heat-resistant materials, which is why it didn't have any soot. "Going forward, our military plans to further advance the related technologies as it moves to weaponise the HGV, a key strategic asset for future security," the ministry said. Hypersonic weapons typically travel at more than five times the speed of sound, often at relatively low altitudes, with analysts noting their main feature as manoeuvrability to hit targets. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country's first [USN:L1N45U08H TEXT:"hypersonic test-firing"] last month, the presidential office said. The rare public showcasing of a missile test by a South Korean president came amid heightened tensions on the Korean Peninsula and a race to develop weapons capable of evading missile defences.

item.title: Red Wings owner responds to fan backlash: ‘I understand it’
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings entered Thursday near the bottom of the NHL standings at 1-3-2 (4 points).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Red Wings entered Thursday near the bottom of the NHL standings at 1-3-2 (4 points). Captain Dylan Larkin requested a trade this summer, and one of their top defensemen remains without a contract. They still don't have a permanent general manager after removing franchise legend Steve Yzerman from the role in July. Through it all, Red Wings owner Chris Ilitch said he understands why fans have begun chants directed at him to "Sell the team." "Fans absolutely have the right to tell us how they feel," Ilitch told reporters Thursday before the Red Wings hosted the Philadelphia Flyers. "This is their team. So I understand fan frustration. I share it, to be frank. My thoughts are that fans want to see our team win on the ice, and I do too. And as the person that's accountable for this franchise, it's why I made the change (in general managers), and it's why I'm so deliberate in our search." Ilitch said the Red Wings are working to hire a president of hockey operations, and he will let that hire decide whether to bring in a general manager under him or her. Shawn Horcoff, the current interim GM, remains a candidate for the full-time role. Ilitch defended the timing of his decision to remove Yzerman, which has had an impact on the Red Wings' ability to get a deal done with restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson before the season began. Horcoff said Wednesday that the Red Wings had "zero interest" in trading Edvinsson amid the elongated negotiations. "I think what is happening, the direction I'm taking this franchise is the right direction," Ilitch said. "It's one of the most important things I can do, and one of the biggest contributions I can have to this franchise is to go out and find an innovative difference-making leader who's going to be able to help us build that championship team again. I'm determined to find the right leadership, and I'm not really looking backwards to say, ‘should this have happened or could that have happened?' I'm looking forward, and very focused on finding our next leader." Ilitch also said that he supported Dylan Larkin, the longtime captain and franchise player who is from the Detroit area and has spent his full NHL career with the club. "I support Dylan. I support every single one of our players on our roster," the owner said. "I do everything I can in terms of resources, support, to make sure that our players can reach their full potential, and that's how our team is going to reach its full potential. And so I support all of our players. Until they're not a Red Wing, they have my full support." Larkin, 30, is a two-time All-Star who has played 813 games for the Red Wings, counting Thursday. He entered Thursday with 277 goals and 368 assists for his career. Edvinsson, 23, was the sixth overall draft pick in 2021 and tallied 19 goals and 41 assists in 175 games over his first four seasons. Horcoff and the Red Wings did ink forward Alex DeBrincat to a seven-year, $91 million contract extension earlier this week. --Field Level Media

item.title: Singapore's September exports rise 68.4% on year
item.description: Singapore's non-oil domestic exports rose by 68.4% in September from a year earlier, government data showed on Friday, a sixth straight month of growth above 20%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Singapore's non-oil domestic exports rose by 68.4% in September from a year earlier, government data showed on Friday, a sixth straight month of growth above 20%. The expansion was driven mainly by non-electronics, primarily the exports of structures of ships and boats, but electronic exports also surged. The export figure was higher than the median forecast of 32.2% growth in a Reuters poll. Electronics exports rose by 107.6% in September from a year earlier, and non-electronics shipments were up 54.2%, Enterprise Singapore said in a statement. Shipments rose to nine of Singapore's top 10 markets, with exports to Hong Kong rising 112.1%. In August, Enterprise Singapore upgraded its forecast for growth this year in non-oil domestic exports to a range of 14% to 16%, from 3% to 5%.

item.title: Taiwan tells its people to shun Chinese anniversary events for revolutionary hero
item.description: Taiwan's government has told its people to shun events in China next month for the anniversary of the birth of a man officially lauded by both Taipei and Beijing for bringing an end to the last imperial dynasty, exposing another historical fault line.
item.dc:creator: Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: Taiwan's government has told its people to shun events in China next month for the anniversary of the birth of a man officially lauded by both Taipei and Beijing for bringing an end to the last imperial dynasty, exposing another historical fault line. China announced last year that it would hold commemorations on November 12 this year for the 160th birthday of Sun Yat-sen, who died in 1925 but helped lead the 1911 revolution that ended centuries of rule by emperors and empresses. Sun then founded the Republic of China, which fled to Taiwan in 1949 after losing a civil war with Mao Zedong's communists, and that remains Taiwan's formal name. Beijing has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control. In a statement late on Thursday, Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said people should not go to China for anniversary events and "echo the Chinese communists' narratives". China's interpretation of Sun "does not stay faithful to historical fact ... It uses these commemorations to promote a narrative of 'opposing Taiwan independence and promoting unification,'" the council said. China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to a request for comment. XI SPOKE AT PREVIOUS COMMEMORATION Beijing's government says Sun is a great national hero and patriot, as well as the forerunner of China's 1949 revolution. China has not detailed what events it will hold next month for the anniversary. In 2016, President Xi Jinping gave a speech saying Sun opposed attempts to "split the country", adding that the "complete reunification of the motherland" was a sacred duty for all Chinese. In Taiwan, Sun is officially considered the "father of the nation" and his portrait hangs in the presidential office, though his "Three Principles of the People" political philosophy is no longer a required school text for children. While Taiwan President Lai Ching-te and his ruling Democratic Progressive Party champion Taiwan's separate identity from China, they have been striking a tougher tone with Beijing on the role of the Republic of China. Taiwan's government has been particularly [USN:L4N45J003 TEXT:"upset"] with Beijing seeking to claim [USN:L4N45M05D TEXT:"credit"] for the victory in World War Two, saying it was the Republic of China government that fought with the allies as the People's Republic of China did not exist then. China says Lai is a "separatist" and has refused to speak with him. Lai says only Taiwan's people can decide their future.

item.title: US probes Omar's decades-old immigration paperwork with eye toward deportation, sources say
item.description: A predawn raid on Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar’s home by federal agents stemmed from an expanding investigation into her US immigration paperwork, three people familiar with the case said this week.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Kristina Cooke
item.content:encoded: A predawn raid on Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar’s home by federal agents stemmed from an expanding investigation into her US immigration paperwork, three people familiar with the case said this week. The investigation appears to center on whether the Somali-born Omar, who has represented a Minnesota district since 2019, or her relatives gave false information upon entering the US as refugees in the mid-1990s or during the process of becoming American citizens. The sealed warrant for [USN:L1N45Y0CB TEXT:"Monday's search"] listed conspiracy, false statements on immigration paperwork and immigration fraud as potential crimes being investigated, one of the people familiar with the matter said. Like the other people, they spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss an ongoing investigation. One of the people familiar with the probe told Reuters that one potential aim could be to strip Omar of her US citizenship and deport her, ideas that both President Donald Trump and his Homeland Security chief have floated. The targeting of a left-wing member of Congress whom Trump has [USN:L4N3ZL27U TEXT:"long attacked in personal and bigoted terms "]has renewed concerns that his administration is using federal law enforcement to punish his political opponents, especially three weeks before an election when Omar is running to retain her seat. Omar has denied wrongdoing, characterizing the raid as an act of “political intimidation.” The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees the immigration enforcement agency, referred questions to the Justice Department. A DOJ spokesperson declined to comment on the Omar investigation. But in a statement, the spokesperson said that US citizenship "must be obtained lawfully and honestly" and the Trump administration would investigate any case where the facts support denaturalization, the legal process of revoking citizenship that was acquired after birth. A spokesperson for Omar had no immediate comment. A RARE STEP Former immigration officials said denaturalization investigations have historically been rare, and it is extremely unusual for them to involve search warrants, as the government should already have the relevant immigration records. "Most of the denaturalization cases that we engaged in related either to very serious international human rights violations, or very serious crimes, such as Nazi war criminals,” said Kerry Doyle, a former deputy general counsel in the Department of Homeland Security during the Biden administration. Agents with Homeland Security Investigations, a branch of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, seized Omar's personal cell phone during the search, according to two of the sources. Federal prosecutors also issued more than a dozen subpoenas, including to at least one of Omar’s relatives, the two people said. One of the people said a sister of Omar spoke voluntarily with federal agents. It was unclear what evidence prosecutors presented to the federal magistrate judge who approved the raid. A coalition of 14 news organizations, including Reuters, asked a federal judge on Thursday to unseal records related to the search. PROTECTIONS FOR CONGRESS The DOJ has traditionally refrained from investigative acts against political figures that are likely to become public within 60 days of an election, particularly if the evidence can be collected after votes are cast. Omar's status as a sitting member of Congress made the timing all the more unusual, and the probe potentially more fraught. Courts have ruled that federal authorities cannot review material related to the legislative acts of a member of Congress, which is protected under the US Constitution. Before approving the search, US Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh ordered screening procedures to prevent such a review, according to three people familiar with the matter. Under the terms of the warrant, prosecutors were supposed to inform Omar's lawyers about the protocol for protecting legislative records, but that has not happened, one of the people said. DENATURALIZATION Omar was 12 when her family arrived in the United States in 1995 after fleeing civil war in Somalia and spending years at a refugee camp in Kenya. She became a naturalized citizen in 2000. Omar's background has been central to her [USN:KCN1N518M TEXT:"political rise"] -- and a consistent target of her right-wing critics. Trump has repeatedly attacked her heritage, her Muslim faith and the Somali community in Minnesota. Asked by the New York Times in January if he thought Omar should lose her US citizenship, Trump replied: "Oh, absolutely." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a conservative podcaster last month there may have been "some illegal activity for them (Omar's family) to come to the United States to begin with" and suggested deportation as a possibility. A naturalized US citizen can lose citizenship if a judge finds it was obtained illegally or through the concealment or willful misrepresentation of material facts. The DOJ has filed at least 164 denaturalization cases in Trump's second term. Between 1990 and 2017, just 11 denaturalization cases were opened on average each year, according to the Immigrant Legal Resource Center.

item.title: Uncertain forecast affects ALCS Game 4 pitching plans for Guardians, Rays
item.description: CLEVELAND -- The Cleveland Guardians have wrested home-field advantage from the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series and taken a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven matchup.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- The Cleveland Guardians have wrested home-field advantage from the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series and taken a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven matchup. Beyond that, little is certain as the teams prepare to play Game 4 on Friday night. Guardians manager Stephen Vogt and Rays counterpart Kevin Cash will not name their starting pitchers until arriving at the ballpark, despite inquiries on the subject. Extended periods of rain are also in the forecast, forcing MLB officials to work on contingency plans if a postponement occurs. The next two games take place in Cleveland before Sunday's scheduled travel day. "Having as much momentum as we can possibly have and being able to feed off of that, it's a lot of fun," said Guardians center fielder Petey Halpin, who hit his first postseason home run on Thursday in Game 3. "We feed off the crowd, feed off the energy. It's great." Halpin's two-run homer in the fifth inning gave Cleveland the lead for good in a 3-2 victory. It continued a breakout postseason for the 24-year-old rookie, who is batting .364 (4-for-11) with an .818 slugging percentage since moving into the lineup for the Guardians' win-or-go-home Game 5 against the Chicago White Sox on Saturday night. In one of the most improbable scenes in recent memory, Halpin unleashed a 25-foot-high bat flip after taking Griffin Jax deep Thursday -- and basked in chants of "Pe-tey" each time he came to the plate or fielded a ball the rest of the afternoon. "The bat flip was maybe a little much, if you ask me, but the moment was so exciting," said Guardians closer Cade Smith. "We're thrilled when stuff like that happens. It's so much fun. Guys are jumping around, giving high-fives, so it's a lot of fun." Cleveland's pitching plan has come together well for potential Games 6 and 7 on the road, which would see Parker Messick and postseason strikeout leader Gavin Williams go on normal rest. One bullpen game and one traditional starter are needed for the next two with Foster Griffin, Joey Cantillo and Slade Cecconi the top candidates to fulfill the starting role. Tanner Bibee is another option, but his poor outing in Game 4 of the AL Division Series against the White Sox hurt his stock. "It is what it is. Our guys are ready to go at all times," Vogt said. "Obviously, with everything up in the air, we're going to be prepared to play. Whatever time, whatever place." Tampa Bay, which won Game 2 at home, made Nick Martinez available to the media Thursday in a postgame press conference, a role generally reserved in the playoffs for the next game's starter. The 36-year-old right-hander pitched 3 2/3 innings and gave up two runs against the New York Yankees when he started Game 3 of the ALDS on Oct. 7. Martinez went 15-6 with a 3.10 ERA in the regular season over 31 starts, but Cash made him a bullpen option earlier in the ALCS. The skipper said he expects "a pretty rain-filled day," which is why he wouldn't commit to Martinez starting Game 4. "The first game, I sat in the bullpen and didn't really like it," Martinez said, chuckling. "I was in the dugout with cleats on the second game. Whatever the team needs, I'm up for it. That's got to be my mentality for the rest of the year." Martinez pitched brilliantly against the Guardians during the regular season. He won both of his starts while permitting just seven hits and one walk over 13 scoreless innings. He added nine strikeouts as Cleveland's batters posted a .159/.178/.182 slash line against him. "We're just going to take it as we go, right?" Martinez said. "Not much you can control about that, so just be ready to go." --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: Progress toward a US-Mexico tariff deal has stalled, WSJ reports
item.description: Progress toward a US-Mexico tariff deal has stalled after opposition from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the talks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Progress toward a US-Mexico tariff deal has stalled after opposition from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the talks. The US and Mexico had been closing in on a deal that would reduce US levies on steel, aluminum and automobiles in return for concessions from Mexico, but progress has slowed due to disagreements over the American levies on vehicles and metals, the report said. Lutnick has opposed significant reductions in the 25% tariff on Mexican automobiles and the 50% levies on steel and aluminum, and he objected to reductions in tariffs on finished products made of steel and aluminum, the Journal added. However, Mexico's deputy trade minister Luis Rosendo Gutierrez told the Journal there was progress in the negotiations, while a US Commerce Department spokesperson told the newspaper the department was in constant dialogue with Mexico on trade. Mexico's ministry of economy and the US Department of Commerce did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

item.title: Fed's Goolsbee on inflation: discouraging, but still some optimism
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that data this week showing stronger-than-expected consumer and producer price inflation has been "discouraging."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that data this week showing stronger-than-expected consumer and producer price inflation has been "discouraging." "I still have some optimism that if the drivers of inflation are things that can go away in short order, whether that's tariffs, whether that's wars in the Middle East and supply disruptions, that's the best scenario," Goolsbee said in an interview on CNN. "If it's coming from overheating demand, from AI data center build out, that's a little more disturbing and we'd have to address that."

item.title: Japan to sidestep 3.5% defence spending target despite US pressure, Asahi reports
item.description: Japan is set to stop short of explicitly adopting a defence spending target of 3.5% of GDP in a planned revision of its national security strategy later this year, despite repeated US calls on allies to meet that benchmark, the Asahi newspaper reported on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan is set to stop short of explicitly adopting a defence spending target of 3.5% of GDP in a planned revision of its national security strategy later this year, despite repeated US calls on allies to meet that benchmark, the Asahi newspaper reported on Friday. The government is instead leaning toward significantly increasing defence-related spending over the next five years, including broader security expenditures, the report said, citing multiple government sources. Tokyo hopes that a demonstrated commitment to strengthening military capabilities will appease Washington, the report added. The defence ministry did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment on the report. According to Asahi, US President Donald Trump's administration has repeatedly urged Japan behind closed doors to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP, describing the level as a global standard for allies. But formally committing to such a target would pose a major fiscal challenge for Tokyo. Defence spending at 3.5% of GDP would exceed 20 trillion yen ($126.52 billion) annually, requiring substantial new funding sources and likely forcing politically sensitive tax increases, Asahi said. ($1 = 158.0800 yen)

item.title: Health Rounds: Glucose monitoring devices for type 2 diabetes benefit even those not on insulin
item.description: Hello Health Rounds readers! Today we highlight a study that found benefits of wearable glucose monitoring devices for all patients with diabetes, regardless of insulin dependence. We also report on a positive trial of a J&J pill in ulcerative colitis, and a discovery about ovaries after menopause.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Lapid
item.content:encoded: Hello Health Rounds readers! Today we highlight a study that found benefits of wearable glucose monitoring devices for all patients with diabetes, regardless of insulin dependence. We also report on a positive trial of a J&J pill in ulcerative colitis, and a discovery about ovaries after menopause. Continuous glucose monitoring benefits all with diabetes The benefits of wearable continuous glucose monitoring devices extend even to patients with diabetes who do not use insulin, a new study found. Until now, the devices have been recommended only for patients receiving insulin. In a six-month trial sponsored by device manufacturer Dexcom (DXCM.O) , 283 adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin received either continuous glucose monitoring with the Dexcom G7 — a coin-size plastic disc worn on the upper arm — or routine care. The average hemoglobin A1c — a measure of average blood sugar levels over time — fell from 8.8% to 7.2% in the monitoring group and from 8.7% to 8.0% in the routine-care group. After accounting for individual risk factors, Dexcom G7 users had a nearly 1% greater reduction in HbA1c level compared to patients getting routine care, researchers reported in The New England Journal of Medicine . Participants using the wearable device also spent approximately five additional hours per day in the glucose target range of 70–180 mg/dL compared with those receiving routine care. The benefit was seen regardless of age, sex, race and ethnicity, body mass index, income, education, health insurance and use of glucose-lowering medications. When the study ended, 97% of participants were still using the monitors, most on a daily basis, the researchers noted. “The consistency of benefit across a broad range of people and treatment regimens supports consideration of the use of a continuous glucose monitor much earlier in type 2 diabetes management before insulin is needed,” study leader Dr. Roy Beck of the Jaeb Center for Health Research in Tampa, Florida, said in a statement. J&J pill succeeds in ulcerative colitis trial Johnson & Johnson's (JNJ.N) [USN:L6N40412G TEXT:"new psoriasis pill"] Icotyde significantly outperformed a placebo as a treatment for ulcerative colitis in a mid-stage trial. Known chemically as icotrokinra, Icotyde is a first-in-class oral peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 protein on immune cells. Previous IL-23 blockers were given intravenously. In the 252-patient trial, participants with moderate to severe active ulcerative colitis received either 400 milligrams of icotrokinra, 200 mg, 100 mg or a placebo, daily. All doses of icotrokinra were superior to placebo for producing a clinical response — a decrease in disease activity and symptoms like rectal bleeding — at week 12, the researchers said. At 400 mg daily, 63% experienced a clinical response. It was 58% in the 200-mg group, 55% in the 100-mg group, and 27% in the placebo group, the researchers reported in The New England Journal of Medicine . The rate of clinical remission at week 12 was also significantly higher with 400 mg than with placebo at 30% versus 11%, as were the rates of symptomatic remission (46% vs 19%) and endoscopic improvement (37% vs 14%). Remissions at week 12 were maintained through 28 weeks of treatment, the researchers said. “Icotrokinra was effective even in hard-to-treat patients who had failed previous drug regimens,” study leader Dr. Maria Abreu of Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles said in a statement. “The fact that the medicine can be taken orally will help us improve the range of options we have for treating patients.” The researchers said they hope to study the drug in patients with Crohn’s disease as J&J looks to expand approvals for the medication. Ovaries keep working after menopause A paradigm-shifting study found human ovaries do not become dormant after menopause, raising questions about whether they play a role in aging and chronic disease. While their reproductive functions end, ovaries remain biologically active for decades and continue to remodel with age, showing increased inflammation and changes in tissue structure, researchers reported in Aging Cell . “In the ovary, we reach a point of no return with respect to fertility in which it's no longer producing eggs, and I would venture to say most people assume those ovaries are just sitting there doing nothing, similar to the appendix,” study co-leader Francesca Duncan of Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine said in a statement. Her team's findings challenge that notion. The researchers studied 28 ovaries obtained from women within 25 years after menopause. Over the decades, some protein levels in the ovaries would go up and some would go down. For example, ovaries from younger postmenopausal women had more proteins involved in maintaining cells and tissue structure, while older ovaries had more proteins associated with inflammation, immune activity and the ongoing breakdown and rebuilding of the tissue surrounding cells. The study also found a molecular link between ovarian aging and cancer. Although all the ovarian tissue in the study appeared normal and cancer-free, some proteins previously associated with ovarian cancer were more abundant in aging ovaries, suggesting that healthy ovarian aging and ovarian cancer share some of the same biological processes. “It's not that all postmenopausal women get ovarian cancer, but we know that the fibrotic inflammatory environment is certainly an environment that cancer cells prefer to home in on,” Duncan said. The findings do not mean healthy ovaries should be removed after menopause, the researchers emphasized. But the discovery could spur research into drugs that "target the aging ovary therapeutically to lower the risk of ovarian cancer" or the development of novel biomarkers of ovarian cancer, Duncan said.

item.title: Google warns suspected China-linked hackers could exploit BeyondTrust flaw
item.description: Google warned on Thursday that organizations should prepare for "potential widespread exploitation" after a new bug was found in US cybersecurity firm BeyondTrust's remote support appliances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Google warned on Thursday that organizations should prepare for "potential widespread exploitation" after a new bug was found in US cybersecurity firm BeyondTrust's remote support appliances. Successful exploitation of the vulnerability gives attackers access to credentials, allows them to arbitrarily upload files and assume control of the host, according to Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant. Here are more details: A suspected China-linked hacking group, known as Armory Castle, had exploited the then-unknown vulnerability in August, a post on Google's blog said The flaw affects BeyondTrust Remote Support, an enterprise tool that allows information technology teams to remotely access and troubleshoot computers and other devices Google says now that the vulnerability has been disclosed, Armory Castle and others may try to exploit it widely, in line with past behavior and urged swift action to either patch or mitigate the vulnerability

item.title: Maple Leafs deal for Canucks F Aatu Raty
item.description: The Vancouver Canucks traded forward Aatu Raty to the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday for forwards Brandon Buhr and Jacob Quillan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Vancouver Canucks traded forward Aatu Raty to the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday for forwards Brandon Buhr and Jacob Quillan. Raty, 23, has tallied one goal through four games to start this season. Last season was his first time playing in more than 33 NHL games; he appeared in 66 contests and contributed four goals and 10 assists. "We want to thank Aatu for all he has done for the organization, and we wish him well in Toronto," Canucks general manager Ryan Johnson said in a release. "By acquiring Jacob and Brandon this move gives our group two new young players to work with as we continue to look for ways to improve our overall depth." A second-round draft pick by the New York Islanders in 2021, Raty only played 12 games for his original franchise before he was dealt to Vancouver as part of the January 2023 trade that sent Bo Horvat to the Isles. Raty has split time between the NHL and AHL for the Canucks. In 118 career NHL games for the Canucks and Islanders, he has amassed 29 points (14 goals, 15 assists) and 42 penalty minutes. He also has won 59.2% of his faceoffs. He has represented Finland in international competition and was part of the nation's 2026 IIHF world champion team. Raty recorded four goals and three assists in 10 games in that tournament. Buhr, 24, has yet to make his NHL debut. He appeared in five games for the Maple Leafs' AHL affiliate last season and had two assists. Quillan, 24, appeared in 24 NHL games for the Leafs across the 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons and registered one goal and two assists. He was scoreless in four appearances this season for the AHL's Toronto Marlies. --Field Level Media

item.title: Shohei Ohtani, back in leadoff spot, ends career-worst homer drought
item.description: After being dropped to No. 6 in the batting order, Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani moved back to the leadoff spot and ended his homer drought on Thursday in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: After being dropped to No. 6 in the batting order, Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani moved back to the leadoff spot and ended his homer drought on Thursday in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series. In the second inning against Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Dustin May, Ohtani belted a two-out, three-run shot, his first long ball since Aug. 18. As the 428-foot blast sailed toward the right field pavilion at Dodger Stadium, Ohtani looked back at the Los Angeles dugout and did an emphatic bat flip before rounding the bases. Ohtani ended a 25-game homer drought, the longest of his career, while producing his first extra-base hit and first RBIs of the 2026 postseason. He had been 4-for-23 (.174) in the playoffs before the home run. Since his most recent homer nearly two months ago against the Colorado Rockies, Ohtani had managed just one RBI. The Milwaukee Brewers won the first three games of the best-of-seven NLCS and can clinch a World Series berth with a Game 4 win. With the Dodgers facing elimination, manager Dave Roberts put Ohtani back atop the order for the first time since the final game of the regular season on Sept. 27. In Los Angeles' 6-2 loss on Wednesday, Ohtani went 1-for-2 with a walk and a hit by pitch. "Just seeing the work the last couple days, I like where his head is at," Roberts said prior to Game 4. "I just really -- I liked the at-bats yesterday, and I felt that trying to shake it up a little bit. Obviously, we haven't performed the way that we're capable of, so to kind of shake it up a little bit, but something that's of somewhat normalcy that our guys are used to." Ohtani, 32, has been bothered by right biceps and left knee injuries for multiple months and his productivity has slipped. When he batted sixth against the Brewers on Wednesday, it marked the first time he had batted so low in a starting lineup since Sept. 19, 2020 -- when the Los Angeles Angels slotted him sixth as the designated hitter against the Texas Rangers. Roberts said he didn't tell Ohtani in advance that he was returning to the leadoff spot. He likes the idea of it possibly jump-starting Ohtani and his struggling troops. "I feel good about him taking five at-bats and giving us our best chance to win and produce runs today," Roberts said of Ohtani before the game. Ohtani is a four-time MVP -- twice with the Angels and twice with the Dodgers -- during nine big league campaigns. He hit three postseason homers in 2024 and eight in 2025 as the Dodgers won back-to-back titles. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rubio urges Lebanon to not return confiscated explosives to Hezbollah, US official says
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun about the confiscation of hundreds of kilograms of explosives from Hezbollah, a US State Department official said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun about the [USN:L1N4610BJ TEXT:"confiscation"] of hundreds of kilograms of explosives from Hezbollah, a US State Department official said on Thursday. Rubio urged Aoun to hold accountable those who ordered, financed and directed the shipment, and "underscored that returning explosives to (Hezbollah) should be out of the question," the US official said. Rubio urged direct military-to-military communication between Lebanese and Israeli forces "for deconfliction," the official added. A Hezbollah lawmaker said earlier the explosives seized last week by Lebanese security forces belonged to his group. The lawmaker, Hassan Fadlallah, said Hezbollah had intended to use the explosives against Israel, whose troops are occupying swathes of Lebanese territory seized in this year's war. A Hezbollah official and a Lebanese security source told Reuters the explosives seized in a car last week were intended to be used in explosive drones targeting Israeli troops. Aoun told Rubio the Lebanese army and security forces were fully carrying out decisions to prevent armed displays, confiscate weapons and combat smuggling, the presidency said, adding Aoun asked Rubio to pressure Israel to halt attacks on southern Lebanese towns and villages. On March 2, the Lebanese government specifically banned Hezbollah's military activities after the movement launched rockets at Israel to back up Tehran, pulling Lebanon into the broader US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28. Tehran subsequently launched its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon during the war have [USN:L1N3ZR14Q TEXT:"killed thousands"] and [USN:L6N3ZY0Q0 TEXT:"displaced millions"]. Under a deal reached through US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks, Beirut vowed to disarm Hezbollah, which would in turn lead to Israeli troops gradually withdrawing from Lebanon. But Hezbollah has refused to disarm as long as Israeli forces remain on Lebanese land and Israel has continued striking southern Lebanon.

item.title: Order to limit Starshield for Ukraine came from inside White House, sources say
item.description: The order to limit a satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations came from inside the White House, according to two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter.
item.dc:creator: Erin Banco, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: The order to limit a satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations came from inside the White House, according to two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter. The officials said leaders at the Defense Department received a message that the SpaceX Starshield service for the Ukrainian military needed to be slowed. The officials, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, did not specify who in the White House made the decision or who was responsible for implementing the order. The Pentagon is the biggest customer of Starshield, which is the military-grade version of the Starlink service. Ukrainian officials said this week that military-grade Starlink receptors [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"stopped working in Ukraine"] when mounted on fast-moving objects, interfering with the performance of Ukrainian drones that rely on them for onboard guidance systems over Ukrainian territory. A person in Ukraine's Defence Ministry said on Thursday that the receptors were now working when in motion, but only at speeds of up to 100 miles per hour (160 kph). US PRESSURES UKRAINE OVER REFINERY ATTACKS The move to temporarily restrict the vital communications system came as President Donald Trump has pressured Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian refineries, which he has blamed for the soaring energy prices that are denting his Republican Party's prospects in the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"November midterm elections"]. But experts say that surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the US-Israeli war with Iran , which brought Iranian attacks on energy facilities and has largely shut the vital Strait of Hormuz. In response to a request for comment about the order to limit Starshield, a senior US official said: "No such request was ever made by the president." The White House did not respond to questions about whether other administration officials might have made the request. Starshield was developed by SpaceX specifically for government and national-security customers, particularly the US Department of Defense. Starshield uses the Starlink constellation as its backbone. Ukrainian officials said the restrictions complicated strike missions against Russian forces and logistics in occupied territory and slowed interceptor drones used to shoot down incoming Russian Shahed drones. Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX, said on X on Wednesday that because Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government, any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment. The Department of Defense and the Ukrainian embassy in Washington also did not respond to requests for comment. DECLINE IN RELATIONS Relations between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated in recent days following a meeting in Miami on October 9 that convened representatives from both countries as well as Europe and the World Bank. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, the Trump administration’s Middle East envoy, struck a tough tone with Ukraine in the meeting, according to a separate person familiar with the matter. They told Ukrainian officials that the US was frustrated with Kyiv's continued strikes on Russian refineries despite repeated requests from Washington to stop. The US delegation also explained Washington's decision to strike a diesel deal with Russia, saying the White House hoped it would [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"soften Moscow's stance"] on peace talks. That deal, under which Russia will supply more than 2.25 million barrels of diesel to US and global markets, has triggered a backlash from some US lawmakers, who say it will give Moscow cash to pursue its war without forcing Russian President Vladimir Putin to make concessions to end the conflict. In the days that followed, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Trump criticized each other, with Zelenskiy calling the US decision on the Russian diesel deal "weak." Trump called for elections in Ukraine and [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"Zelenskiy's ouster"]. Behind the scenes, American officials threatened to stop providing intelligence to Kyiv about Russian missile launches that Ukraine uses to thwart attacks, as Reuters previously reported. Trump said on Tuesday Washington was [USN:L1N45Z0GP TEXT:"still sharing intelligence"] with Ukraine. Following the move to restrict Ukraine's access to Starshield, the Ukrainians made calls on Tuesday and Wednesday to find answers from senior officials at the White House, State Department and Pentagon, a senior Ukrainian official said, adding that Kyiv was told it was a White House decision. The Pentagon has spent billions of dollars on the Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024.

item.title: Indonesian rescue centre takes in more orangutans as fires rage
item.description: In the jungles of Indonesian Borneo, a rehabilitation centre is taking in more orangutans as the country's worst wildfires in a decade sweep through the forest home of the critically endangered animals.
item.dc:creator: Willy Kurniawan, Yuddy Budiman
item.content:encoded: In the jungles of Indonesian Borneo, a rehabilitation centre is taking in more orangutans as the country's worst wildfires in a decade sweep through the forest home of the critically endangered animals. The intense [USN:L4N44O09W TEXT:"wildfires"], burning mainly on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra, began in July and could continue until November, aggravated by a severe El Niño weather pattern, the government has warned. "I think so far this looks quite similar to the 2015 fires," said Karmele Llano Sanchez, co-founder of Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI), who has worked in Indonesia for more than 20 years. "It's possible that in the months to come, they (the orangutans) will also be affected by not having enough to eat, not having enough room, enough habitat, and starvation." The world's three species of orangutan are native only to Borneo and Sumatra. YIARI, in the Ketapang region of Indonesia's West Kalimantan province, is now looking after 90 orangutans, after rescuing 49 since August, foundation spokesperson Heribertus Suciadi said. Over the last three years, the centre rescued three to five animals a year, he added. The fires and haze have shrouded parts of Borneo, which also includes the Malaysian states of Sarawak and Sabah, in a hazardous smog that has also spread to Singapore and the Malaysian peninsula, forcing some schools to close and causing a spike in respiratory illnesses. Sampurna, an orangutan that [USN:L1N44R01J TEXT:"Reuters encountered"] in August, was found gasping for air and writhing on the ground in a palm oil plantation. Sampurna died on August 30, the forestry ministry said last month. Sanchez, who performed the necropsy on the great ape, said Sampurna died less than 12 hours after being rescued and had very dark lungs owing to respiratory problems, likening them to those of a heavy smoker. From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares (500,000 acres) in Indonesia. No official data for subsequent months has been released, but non-governmental organisations estimate fires have burned at least 600,000 hectares more since. In 2015, fires burned nearly 960,000 hectares, forestry ministry data showed. "I think in general, what we see is that these orangutans that were surviving in these fragments of forest, and the forest fragments are becoming smaller and smaller and smaller," Sanchez said. RESCUE MISSIONS Once YIARI volunteers receive reports of orangutan sightings, they use a drone to determine the areas ravaged by the fires and whether orangutans were living there, Heribertus said. Equipped with tranquilisers, rescuers then drive for hours to the burned forest to find the orangutans, sometimes using a net to capture the apes before taking them to safety. The foundation has more than 200 staff, including firefighters and veterinarians. "Fires are occurring in many areas. As a result, the orangutans are being displaced into plantations," said Relly Susanto, a YIARI patroller. On a recent August day at the YIARI centre, orangutans swung through the trees and walked on vines, as youngsters ate fruit next to their mothers. While there is no escape from the smoke even at YIARI, the centre is not currently at risk from the fires themselves and some of the rescued orangutans have been [USN:L4N45X00X TEXT:"returned to the wild"] in safer locations. At the moment, YIARI has enough capacity to take in the orangutans, Sanchez said. But with the fires showing little sign of abating, she is not sure how long that will last. "It's difficult to quantify how many orangutans will need to be rescued," she said. "One of our concerns is whether we'll have enough capacity to really get all of these rescued orangutans into the facility." Click on https://bit.ly/4hWQmeq to see the related photo essay.

item.title: Global EV sales fall 2% in September, ending six-month growth streak
item.description: Global demand for electric vehicles fell 2% in September, ending six consecutive months of growth, as record sales in Europe were not enough to offset sharp declines in North America and China, data from UK-based research firm Benchmark Mineral Intelligence showed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Amir Orusov
item.content:encoded: Global demand for electric vehicles fell 2% in September, [USN:L6N4520P0 TEXT:"ending"] six consecutive months of growth, as record sales in Europe were not enough to offset sharp declines in North America and China, data from UK-based research firm Benchmark Mineral Intelligence showed on Friday. The data highlights growing divergence across major EV markets. Europe is benefiting from strong consumer demand and policy support, while China's domestic market remains weak and North America continues to feel the impact of the expiration of US federal EV tax credits at the end of September 2025. Global EV sales slid to 2.15 million vehicles in September, while year-to-date volumes are up 3% at 15.5 million units "Europe had its strongest month on record, with almost 600,000 EVs sold in September, 10% above the previous high set in June," BMI data manager Charles Lester said North American sales fell 44%, the steepest monthly decline this year, reflecting the strong year-ago period when buyers rushed to dealerships before the tax credits expired From the fourth quarter, these comparisons will ease as they lap the post-tax-credit slump, Lester said Sales in China dropped 18% to 1.11 million vehicles, prompting carmakers to increasingly rely on exports

Nos últimos dias, Lula também anunciou o [USN:L1N45Z0NK TEXT:"perdão"] de dívidas para microempreendedores, juntamente com subsídios de R$5.000 destinados ao mesmo público. Na semana passada, seu governo ampliou os subsídios aos [USN:L1N45V0MB TEXT:"combustíveis"], alegando a necessidade de proteger os consumidores do aumento dos preços globais do petróleo, enquanto, há menos de um mês, aumentou os benefícios do [USN:L1N4590J2 TEXT:"Bolsa Família"] em 15%. Com o objetivo de aliviar a pressão sobre as finanças das famílias, o governo também anunciou que realizará um leilão para comprar e reestruturar dívidas domésticas utilizando recursos públicos. item.title: Mexico shrinks protected area as world's rarest porpoise battles extinction
item.description: Mexico's president said on Thursday a drastic reduction in the protected area for the near-extinct vaquita marina, the world's smallest porpoise, will help fishing communities, although critics fear the move threatens the species' survival.
item.dc:creator: Ana Martinez, Sarah Morland
item.content:encoded: Mexico's president said on Thursday a drastic reduction in the protected area for the near-extinct vaquita marina, the world's smallest porpoise, will help fishing communities, although critics fear the move threatens the species' survival. Mexico's government this week reduced the area where fishermen cannot use gillnets – long walls of nylon mesh – by 86% to 1,562 square kilometers (603 square miles), about the size of Greater London. The prior agreement had protected an area similar to the size of the US state of Connecticut. President Claudia Sheinbaum said the new scope aimed to protect biodiversity in the Gulf of California while also allowing fishermen to make a better living. Authorities said the measure took into account proposals by the International Committee for the Recovery of the Vaquita, a government advisory body. Lorenzo Rojas-Bracho, a Mexican marine biologist and leading vaquita expert who took part in the committee, said he hoped a smaller area could concentrate efforts to save the mammal. "It is difficult to enforce a ban over a very large area, which includes vast areas with no recent records of vaquitas," Rojas-Bracho told Reuters. "If you lose a ring you don't search your entire house, you focus on where you lost it." Scientists estimated last year there were just 7 to 10 vaquitas left, including at least one calf. The population has collapsed from around 600 in 1997, largely due to illegal fishing targeting totoaba, whose swim bladders are highly prized in Chinese medicine and can fetch up to $10,000 in Asia. Rojas-Bracho said that if no more vaquitas are killed, the remaining handful of porpoises would have a good chance of repopulating the species. Conservation expert Gerardo Ceballos, a biologist at the National Autonomous University of Mexico, was less optimistic. "What's happening to the vaquita is a death foretold," he said. "We've reduced the vaquita's protected area without actually having the technical or logistical capacity to enforce regulations there; we're giving in to pressure from interested groups so a larger area can be exploited." Ceballos said a very minimal investment from Mexico's government would ensure the vaquita's protection. As things currently stood, however, he believed the porpoise was on the path to extinction. "If the vaquita goes extinct it won't solve insecurity or poverty or any of the local problems. And Mexico would lose an icon," he said. "If actions are taken, there is a possibility, a hope. And we must keep working with hope."

item.title: Lula pledges free weekend transit nationwide as Brazil runoff nears
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said on Thursday he will send Congress a constitutional amendment guaranteeing free weekend public transport nationwide, the latest in a series of voter-friendly measures less than two weeks before Brazil's presidential runoff.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said on Thursday he will send Congress a constitutional amendment guaranteeing free weekend public transport nationwide, the latest in a series of voter-friendly measures less than two weeks before Brazil's presidential runoff. In a video posted on social media, Lula said the program would be funded through congressional budget earmarks. The president did not say when exactly he would send the proposal. Lula, who [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"unexpectedly trailed"] right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in the first round, remains narrowly behind in polls ahead of the October 25 runoff. The proposal adds to a string of measures aimed at boosting household purchasing power, particularly among lower-income Brazilians, as record indebtedness and rising debt-servicing costs squeeze family finances. The measures have also raised fiscal concerns. With no offsetting cuts announced, economists warn an expanding pre-election giveaway package could stoke investor anxiety over public finances, lifting borrowing costs and adding pressure to Brazil's [USN:L1N45M0ES TEXT:"debt trajectory"]. On Wednesday, the [USN:L1N46100U TEXT:"Senate approved"] a government-backed measure ending Brazil's six-days-on, one-day-off work schedule, providing Lula a key legislative win. In recent days, Lula has also announced debt forgiveness for small entrepreneurs, along with 5,000 Brazilian reais grants targeting the same audience. Last week, his government [USN:L6N45V0S9 TEXT:"expanded fuel subsidies"], citing the need to shield consumers from rising global oil prices, while less than a month ago it raised [USN:L1N4590JP TEXT:"Bolsa Familia benefits"] by 15%. Seeking to ease pressure on household finances, the government also announced it [USN:L1N45H0UN TEXT:"would hold an auction"] to buy and restructure household debt using government proceeds. Another recent move was a ban on online betting operators, amid concerns that growing gambling spending has strained household budgets and fueled indebtedness.

item.content:encoded: The US FDA on Thursday warned of a potentially high-risk issue involving certain Edwards Lifesciences (EW.N) delivery systems used in transcatheter mitral valve replacement after one death and one serious injury. The FDA said Edwards Lifesciences had asked customers to remove affected products from use and return them after receiving three reports of balloons bursting during inflation. The company reported one death and one serious injury associated with the issue as of October 5. The affected devices are certain Commander M delivery systems used with Edwards' SAPIEN M3 transcatheter mitral valve replacement system, which received US approval in December 2025. The FDA said balloon bursts could block blood vessels or prevent retrieval of the device, potentially requiring additional procedures, including surgery, in patients generally considered unsuitable for surgery.
