item.title: Rotting meat smell sparks protest at Mexico's screwworm sterile-fly plant
item.description: A rotten smell hanging over a town in Mexico's southern Chiapas state drove residents into the streets on Thursday to demand the removal of a sterile-fly plant at the center of the US-Mexican fight against the flesh-eating New World screwworm parasite.
item.dc:creator: Jose Torres, Cassandra Garrison
item.content:encoded: A rotten smell hanging over a town in Mexico's southern Chiapas state drove residents into the streets on Thursday to demand the removal of a sterile-fly plant at the center of the US-Mexican fight against the flesh-eating New World screwworm parasite. Residents in Metapa de Dominguez compared the odor to rotting meat and spoiled food, describing it as “pungent in your nose and mouth” and causing nausea. The smell, once concentrated around the plant, could now be detected farther away, particularly when winds carried it across the town, protesters said. The odor had reached schools near the plant and disrupted classes. "We don't care about the investment they made. What we want is for this plant to leave here, because the smell coming over the town is too much," said truck driver Mercedes Becerra de la Cruz. The complaints come less than four months after Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins [USN:L6N42X14F TEXT:"inaugurated"] the facility on June 27. The US Department of Agriculture invested $21 million toward the $51 million facility, part of a broader effort to halt a screwworm outbreak that disrupted the cross-border cattle trade. Sterile flies are the main defense against screwworm, a parasite whose larvae burrow into the living flesh of cattle and other warm-blooded animals and can kill them if untreated. Eradicated from the US decades ago, the pest has surged north from Central America through Mexico, prompting Washington to impose a more than year-long ban on Mexican cattle imports. The Metapa plant is expected eventually to produce 100 million sterile flies a week. Mexico has recorded nearly 48,000 cases of screwworm in the current outbreak and the United States 53. Inside the Metapa plant, millions of flies are bred each week, their larvae fed a carefully formulated mixture of egg, milk and powdered hemoglobin that mimics the nutrient-rich conditions of a wound. The flies are sterilized before being released by the millions to mate with wild females without producing offspring, gradually suppressing the population. Outside its walls, residents said daily life has increasingly been shaped by an overpowering odor that drifts into surrounding neighborhoods and schools. "We need the federal government to respond and have the plant relocated. It is far too close, right in the middle of the town," said 49-year-old homemaker Rosalba Merida Herrera. "For the sake of our children and our elderly, we are asking them to look at the situation, as this issue is now affecting the entire town." A spokesperson for Mexico's Agriculture Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Petrolera GeoPark incrementa producción en 3er trimestre, planea perforar hasta 8 pozos en Colombia en 4to trimestre
item.description: La producción promedio consolidada de petróleo y gas de GeoPark aumentó un 2,6% en el tercer trimestre a 27.973 boepd, frente al segundo trimestre, reveló el jueves la compañía en una actualización operacional.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La producción promedio consolidada de petróleo y gas de GeoPark (GPRK.N) aumentó un 2,6% en el tercer trimestre a 27.973 boepd, frente al segundo trimestre, reveló el jueves la compañía en una actualización operacional. "GeoPark tuvo un sólido desempeño operacional en el tercer trimestre de 2026, respaldado por la continuidad de las actividades de desarrollo y exploración en sus principales activos en Colombia, incluido el descubrimiento de Milano 1X, y por la puesta en producción de cinco pozos en Vaca Muerta", precisó la empresa en un comunicado. "En paralelo, la compañía avanzó en su siguiente fase de crecimiento, con progresos hacia el inicio de su campaña de factory drilling en Argentina y la preparación de sus operaciones en Venezuela", agregó. GeoPark anunció que planea la perforación de 7 a 8 pozos brutos durante el cuarto trimestre en Colombia. Entre julio y septiembre GeoPark -controlado por el magnate Jaime Gilinski-, reportó 8 equipos en operación (3 de perforación y 5 de workover), 8 pozos perforados y completados en Colombia, y 5 pozos fracturados y en producción en Argentina. A finales de septiembre, el director ejecutivo de GeoPark anunció que planea invertir 7.000 millones de dólares en el vasto yacimiento petrolífero venezolano de Bare para aumentar la producción de crudo allí a unos 90.000 barriles diarios (bpd) para el año 2038, frente a los 11.000 actuales. item.title: US judge tosses Trump administration lawsuit over New York City 'sanctuary' laws
item.description: A federal judge on Thursday threw out a Trump administration lawsuit that sought to block New York City laws limiting cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, finding the government did not have a valid basis to sue.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Thursday threw out a Trump administration lawsuit that sought to block New York City laws limiting cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, finding the government did not have a valid basis to sue. US District Judge Ramon Reyes in Brooklyn said President Donald Trump’s administration could not challenge a city law barring police from detaining immigrants at the request of federal authorities because that practice is already prohibited by state law. The judge also said city laws restricting local authorities from sharing release dates, whereabouts or other custody information about immigrants were valid because federal law does not require state and local governments to share that information. Reyes rejected the administration’s arguments that federal law superseded the challenged New York City laws, finding the federal government could not force local governments to assist with immigration enforcement. The administration filed the lawsuit in New York federal court in July 2025 as part of its campaign against so-called sanctuary city policies, which aim to shield immigrants from Trump’s mass deportation campaign. The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling.

item.title: UN chief frontrunner Rebeca Grynspan says UN has 'become too risk-averse'
item.description: The United Nations has become too risk-averse and its next leader must be prepared to bear the cost of diplomatic failure and try again, Rebeca Grynspan, the frontrunner to be the next UN chief, told Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Antoni Slodkowski
item.content:encoded: The United Nations has become too risk-averse and its next leader must be prepared to bear the cost of diplomatic failure and try again, Rebeca Grynspan, the frontrunner to be the next UN chief, told Reuters on Thursday. She spoke ahead of another Security Council poll on Friday to gauge support for a new secretary-general to succeed Antonio Guterres, whose second five-year term ends on December 31. Grynspan said the UN must also cut jobs, curb bureaucracy and stop agencies duplicating work, arguing that cost-cutting alone would not revive an institution struggling with shrinking resources and declining political clout. “I think that the UN has become too risk-averse,” Grynspan said. “You are the one that has to take the cost of rejection, the cost of failure, and try again. That's the job of the UN.” SHE URGES A MORE PROACTIVE UN Grynspan, 70, a former Costa Rican vice president, called for a more proactive UN after the 193-member body was largely sidelined in wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and as it faces pressure from US President Donald Trump's administration to cut costs. "Cost cutting is not enough. Yes, you can cut costs and make everything worse. If you don't reform, you will do everything worse than before. That's why I talk about refocusing," Grynspan, an economist, told Reuters. Pointing to her tenure as head of the UN Conference on Trade and Development, Grynspan said she cut 20% of posts while sharpening its focus. US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz has criticized what he called bureaucratic " bloat " and duplication at the UN and called for a clearer focus on peacekeeping. Grynspan said she shared Waltz's concerns: "Some consolidation and rethinking of how to carry a mandate is necessary in many of the fields that have been expanding in the UN." She said she would appoint a person inside her office to "impose the discipline that is necessary for mandate implementation." Grynspan pointed to [USN:L1N3B31L4 TEXT:"her role in negotiations"] over [USN:L1N37D31Y TEXT:"the 2022 Black Sea Grain Initiative"] as a model for handling conflicts involving a permanent Security Council member. Russia withdrew from the agreement in 2023 and [USN:S8N3PT07G TEXT:"complained that key parts"] of the deal were never implemented. “We didn't go to the press ... It was quiet diplomacy that worked,” she said. “This is not about being able to have total harmony in the international affairs ... it's about doing good.” Grynspan said the UN already had the expertise, information and presence on the ground needed to play a larger diplomatic role but needed leadership capable of bringing those resources together. “Peacemaking has to be at the center of the efforts of the UN,” she said, citing a rise in deadly interstate conflicts and calling for greater emphasis on mediation as well as prevention. Grynspan also called for greater flexibility in peacekeeping, saying the secretary-general should work closely with the Security Council's five permanent members to find alternative models when traditional peacekeeping is not viable. Pointing to the multinational support mission in Haiti, she said: “Why should we be so defensive? Why should it be only a UN peacekeeping force? ... Let's try to make Haiti work and learn from the experience.” 'GAME NOT OVER' Grynspan, who will become the first female secretary-general in the UN's history if she wins, has come out ahead in four out of five informal straw polls, [USN:L1N45T0L0 TEXT:"obtaining nine votes"] in favor last week, according to diplomats close to the process. Securing the recommendation requires at least nine positive votes out of the 15 countries, and no "discourage" votes from the five permanent members: the US, China, Russia, France, and Britain. Friday's poll will for the first time use color-coded ballots revealing whether a veto power opposes a candidate. Grynspan said she was the only candidate who has consistently reached nine votes in her favor, but she "wouldn't be surprised" if she got a discouraging vote from a veto power. She said such opposition has been overcome in past races. Diplomats at the UN say several senior figures, including former and current foreign ministers and country leaders, are seriously considering entering the race. Grynspan said she expected new names could enter the race after the Friday vote and added: "The game is not over -- we will have to continue working."

item.title: Shooter kills four at Oregon elementary school before being shot dead by community member
item.description: A 16-year-old shooter opened fire on Thursday at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killing four people including three children, before being killed by an armed member of the community who had pursued the assailant into the school, police said.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Trotta, Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: A 16-year-old shooter opened fire on Thursday at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killing four people including three children, before being killed by an armed member of the community who had pursued the assailant into the school, police said. The shooter entered Silver Rail Elementary School by firing through locked doors, police said, without offering any details beyond the suspect's age. The dead were children aged 5, 8 and 11 and one teacher. In addition, a 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to hospital with critical injuries, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz told a press conference. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek, appearing at the same briefing, thanked the community member who "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life." "No parent should have to have this kind of day, and no community should have to live through this kind of day. And as we learn more about the children and the adults who have been killed or injured, and their families and their loved ones, we are going to do a lot of crying, and we are going to cry together, and we're probably going to cry privately," Kotek said. Krantz said the community member, whom he did not identify, saw the suspect enter the school and pursued him. School shootings have become a recurring feature of American life, including high-profile attacks such as those at Columbine High School in 1999, Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012, Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in 2018, and Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, in 2022. Each shooting revives debates over gun laws in a country where gun rights are protected under the Constitution's second amendment. Gun rights advocates have argued for arming teachers as a means of defense. POLICE TRAINED FOR MASS SHOOTING Krantz said every Bend police officer went through a full day of active shooter training in August. "Unfortunately, this is something we train for on a regular basis, and we must," Krantz said. "This is going to be a long investigation." Thursday's shooting took place in Bend, a city of about 100,000 people in rural central Oregon, 175 miles (280 km) southeast of Portland, in the Oregon high desert adjacent to the Deschutes National Forest. Silver Rail Elementary School serves kindergarten through fifth grade, roughly ages 5 to 11, and has about 450 students and 40 staff members, officials said. Gun control advocate Gabrielle Giffords, a former congresswoman who survived a mass shooting in 2011, said in a statement she was "heartbroken" by the shooting in Bend. "This cannot continue to be a reality in our country. Leaders at every level must step up and act,” Giffords said. Emergency responders received a call at 12:59 p.m. PDT (1959 GMT) from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by someone with a long gun, Krantz said. In the minutes afterwards, dozens of calls were received saying the shooter had entered the school, Krantz said. Law enforcement immediately directed the school to go into lockdown, he said. Officers arrived at 1:02 p.m. and moments later an officer reported the suspect had been shot, Krantz said. Police entered and confirmed the suspect was dead, he said.

item.title: Vantagem de Flávio sobre Lula diminui para 47% a 45%, mostra Datafolha
item.description: A vantagem do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) sobre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) diminuiu no segundo turno da disputa pelo Planalto, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira, ainda que as variações registradas estejam dentro da margem de erro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A vantagem do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) sobre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) diminuiu no segundo turno da disputa pelo Planalto, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira, ainda que as variações registradas estejam dentro da margem de erro. Flávio tem 47% das intenções de voto, enquanto Lula soma 45%, segundo o levantamento. Na semana passada, o placar estava em 49% a 45% a favor do senador. Como a margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais, os dois candidatos continuam em situação de empate técnico. Os indecisos somam 2% (eram 1% na pesquisa anterior), enquanto aqueles que dizem que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum candidato chegam a 6% (eram 5%). Em votos válidos, quando não são considerados os votos brancos e nulos e os indecisos, Flávio tem 51% contra 49% de Lula. Na semana passada, o placar era 52% a 48%. Flávio venceu o primeiro turno da disputa pelo Planalto no início do mês com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. O segundo turno será realizado no próximo dia 25. O levantamento desta quinta é o primeiro do Datafolha após manifestações de apoio a Lula em várias cidades do país, a maior delas em São Paulo no último domingo, com a presença do próprio presidente. Ainda assim, os números não mostraram crescimento da sua candidatura nas intenções de voto. Já Flávio registrou uma desidratação dentro da margem de erro que parece ter ido para os indecisos e votos brancos e nulos. O Datafolha também apontou que a rejeição do presidente se manteve em 46%, enquanto a rejeição do senador oscilou para 44%, ante 43% na semana passada. A pesquisa mostrou ainda que 50% desaprovam o governo (ante 49%), enquanto a parcela dos que aprovam se manteve em 48%. Já a avaliação do governo é ruim/péssima para 41% (era 40%), continua ótima/boa para 35% e está regular para 23% (ante 24%). O Datafolha ouviu 2.520 pessoas entre terça e quarta-feira.

item.title: Bolsonaro's lead over Lula narrows ahead of Brazil runoff, Datafolha poll shows
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro continues to slightly lead President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva heading to the October 25 election runoff, but the gap has narrowed, a Datafolha poll showed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro continues to slightly lead President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva heading to the October 25 election runoff, but the gap has narrowed, a Datafolha poll showed on Thursday. The senator, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, would receive 47% of the vote compared with 45% for the president, according to the poll. Last week, a Datafolha poll showed the younger Bolsonaro leading Lula 49% to 45%. The poll's result still represents a technical tie as the margin of error is plus or minus 2 percentage points 6% of the respondents said they would cast a blank vote, and undecided voters made up 2%, the poll showed In valid votes, which exclude blank votes and undecided voters, Bolsonaro leads Lula 51% to 49% Datafolha surveyed 2,520 people between October 13-14 The younger Bolsonaro [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"surprisingly led"] Lula in the first-round vote earlier this month

item.title: Fed's Hammack warns inflation expectations deterioration could require Fed response
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said on Thursday the Fed might need to hike interest rates more aggressively if there were to be a notable deterioration in the public’s inflation expectations.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said on Thursday the Fed might need to hike interest rates more aggressively if there were to be a notable deterioration in the public’s inflation expectations. “What I worry about is, if you get this inflationary mindset, if you get these expectations that these price pressures become more and more persistent, it makes it much harder for monetary policy to do the work that we need to do, and we might need to move even more than if you don't have an inflationary mindset set in,” Hammack said at an event held by Goldman Sachs in New York. Hammack did not give firm guidance about what the current situation means for monetary policy, but the official, who holds a role on the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, has been a strong and early supporter of the central bank countering high inflation pressures with rate rises. The Fed raised its interest rate target by a quarter percentage point to between 3.75% and 4% last month and is widely expected to raise rates again by the end of the year. Inflation data released this week showed worse-than-expected price pressures, which caused some market watchers to increase the odds that the Fed might raise rates at the FOMC meeting on October 27-28. Hammack’s comments on Thursday were among the last public remarks scheduled by central bankers ahead of the quiet period that precedes the month-end meeting. Markets are closely watching a speech scheduled for late Thursday by Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh to see if he offers any monetary policy clues. Hammack also said in her appearance that financial conditions seem roughly neutral right now amid investments in things like technology that are going full speed ahead despite rising borrowing costs. “I'm not feeling that there's restraint coming from financial conditions at this…point in time,” the official said.

item.title: MSCI gets set to remove Indonesia from global indexes, sparks market slide to six-year low
item.description: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, according to MSCI, and the index provider said it intends to cut it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, a major setback that sent money fleeing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, according to MSCI, and the index provider said it intends to cut it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, a major setback that sent money fleeing. In a surprise move, MSCI said on Friday it would put Indonesia on a path to "standalone" status, which was worse than previously flagged, and extended its review of the market by seven months to June 2027. Jakarta stocks (.JKSE) , already the world's worst performers this year, plunged 10% to a six-year low in early trading, while the rupiah slid 0.6% to 18,000 per US dollar, its weakest level since August. Indonesian equities have struggled since January when MSCI froze Indonesia in its indexes and threatened a downgrade to "frontier" status because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour. On Friday, MSCI said reforms to address those problems have not made sufficient progress and that even a downgrade to frontier wouldn't reflect the severity of issues. Instead, it proposed to downgrade Indonesia to "standalone" status, which would exclude Indonesian stocks from global indexes tracked by billions of dollars in passive investment, forcing funds that follow or are ranked against the indexes to sell. "Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction," MSCI said. "Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia's continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate," it said. "Feedback from market participants suggests that a reclassification to frontier markets would not properly recognize the depth of the market problems." The Indonesia Stock Exchange said it has taken concrete steps to enhance transparency and integrity in the country's capital market, and CEO Jeffrey Hendrik said in a statement he would request further clarification on the basis for the announcement. Coming a month ahead of a scheduled review, MSCI's statement stunned investors and Jakarta officials, with the chief of Indonesia's financial regulator Friderica Widyasari Dewi saying she did not expect the announcement following a meeting this week. Finance minister Suahasil Nazara, who chairs the country's financial stability board, did not immediately reply to a request for comment on the MSCI announcement. Angus Mackintosh, an ASEAN specialist at Aletheia Capital in Singapore, said the move does not reflect the health of the vast majority of listed companies or indeed the Indonesian economy, and "grouping Indonesia with Lebanon, Palestine, and Argentina does not make sense." "This is a wake-up call for Indonesia," he said. DOWNGRADE PLANNED FOR MID-2027 MSCI's move seemed heavy-handed given the steps Indonesia has taken to [USN:L6N42W0D2 TEXT:"address issues"] around market transparency and increase the free-float requirement for listed firms, Mackintosh said. The main problem, he said, is Indonesia's "failure to sanction those obviously involved in stock manipulation". MSCI said it will run a consultation with market participants for a downgrade to "standalone" status until April 2027 and then proceed with reclassification unless it finds clear evidence of improvement in market governance and function. Standalone markets are not included in MSCI's emerging or frontier index products, which are tracked by passive funds and treated as performance benchmarks for other fund managers. MSCI says reclassification to standalone status may occur in the case of severe deterioration in market accessibility or size and liquidity, with the most recent example being Argentina. Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, Singapore, called the move a surprise, noting the prospect of a standalone status could encourage index-linked investors to further de-risk. "But for Indonesia, in our view, the bigger concern is less the direct impact on equities and more the potential pressure on the currency from foreign outflows." Indonesia has faced a series of setbacks this year, with [USN:L4N3Z114D TEXT:"Moody's"] and [USN:L1N3ZS06T TEXT:"Fitch"] cutting their sovereign rating outlooks to negative, citing reduced policymaking credibility. The benchmark Jakarta stock index (.JKSE) has fallen more than 30% this year, making it the worst-performing equity market in the world, with net selling by foreign investors at $4.7 billion worth of shares.

item.title: Investors temper Anthropic IPO valuation expectations over revenue growth slowdown, sources say
item.description: Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter said, amid broader concerns over the ballooning cost of financing AI.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn, Anirban Sen
item.content:encoded: Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter said, amid broader concerns over the ballooning cost of financing AI. Some investors who attended [USN:L6N4601AA TEXT:"Anthropic's investor day"] on Wednesday in San Francisco discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, three of the people said, a significant step down from the roughly $2 trillion valuation that investors had previously expected for the November share sale. At Wednesday's meeting, Anthropic told prospective IPO investors that its third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis during the quarter. While those numbers assuaged some concerns about the massive costs of developing AI systems, some investors were disappointed by the slowing sequential growth rate in the latest quarter, as Anthropic's revenue more than doubled from the first quarter to $11.6 billion in the second quarter, the people added. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly on the matter. Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A cooler reception for Anthropic's IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale's success, followed by [USN:L6N45407M TEXT:"OpenAI's potential listing"] next year. BELLWETHER IPO The concerns from investors come as a tech selloff is roiling global financial markets and has hurt AI infrastructure companies, chipmakers and so-called neocloud providers that rent computing power for AI broadly. Shares and bonds of Nvidia (NVDA.O) -backed CoreWeave (CRWV.O) [USN:L4N46111C TEXT:" tumbled on Thursday"], reflecting growing investor concern about an AI buildout that is increasingly being financed with borrowed money. A disappointing share sale for Anthropic could further add to investor worries about the AI buildout. The IPO market has suffered [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"some setbacks"] recently, after data center operator SB Energy decided to delay its listing last month, while nuclear technology company Holtec Nuclear [USN:L4N4581N0 TEXT:"pulled its plans to go public"]. During Wednesday's meeting at Anthropic's headquarters in San Francisco, attendees, mostly the company's most prominent investors, met with CEO Dario Amodei and finance chief Krishna Rao. The Information earlier reported that investors were considering a lower valuation. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic's president, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. The company's rapid growth has been underpinned by Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Amazon (AMZN.O) , which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as AI competitors. Last year, Anthropic's revenue surged twelvefold to nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, excluding writedowns of various liabilities mostly tied to previous fundraising, Reuters [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"reported "]last month. In its IPO prospectus seen exclusively by Reuters in September, Anthropic laid out a vision that AI will transform the global economy more profoundly than industrialization, electricity and the internet, even as it reported a loss of $42 billion in 2025 and projected more spending for the upcoming AI buildout. The company has committed to spending [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"at least $518 billion"] over a decade for cloud services, computing and infrastructure.

item.title: TSE proíbe Meta de restringir conteúdo eleitoral e favorecer Lula ou Flávio com ferramenta de IA
item.description: O ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), proibiu nesta quinta-feira que a Meta restrinja sem justificativa o alcance da divulgação de conteúdos político-eleitorais relacionados às campanhas do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) até o final do segundo turno.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: O ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), proibiu nesta quinta-feira que a Meta restrinja sem justificativa o alcance da divulgação de conteúdos político-eleitorais relacionados às campanhas do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) até o final do segundo turno. Bellizze também determinou que a Meta AI, ferramenta de inteligência artificial da empresa que funciona como um Chatbot não favoreça qualquer das duas candidaturas na produção de conteúdos eleitorais. Em caso de descumprimento, segundo a decisão vista pela Reuters, poderá estabelecer multa diária de R$ 500 mil. Procurada na noite desta quinta-feira, a Meta -- companhia dona das redes sociais Instagram, WhatsApp e Facebook -- disse que não vai comentar. REUNIÃO Representantes da Meta disseram mais cedo nesta quinta ao TSE que estavam trabalhando no aperfeiçoamento de filtros da Meta AI, o assistente de inteligência artificial desenvolvido pela companhia, informou a corte eleitoral após reunião entre as partes. Segundo comunicado divulgado pelo TSE, o presidente e o vice-presidente do tribunal, Kassio Nunes Marques e André Mendonça, reuniram-se com representantes da Meta (META.O) "para debater as ferramentas utilizadas pela empresa que podem contribuir para o período eleitoral brasileiro". O encontro ocorreu um dia após a campanha à reeleição de Lula [USN:L1N46013H TEXT:"recorrer"] ao TSE e até a Organização dos Estados Americanos (OEA) acusando a big tech de usar inteligência artificial e algoritmos para favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro. O TSE disse, no comunicado desta quinta-feira, que a preocupação é promover uma “paridade de armas” entre os candidatos para que o eleitor possa escolher livremente. "Segundo a empresa (Meta), nesta semana, as duas campanhas foram impactadas pela geração de conteúdos de inteligência artificial considerados inadequados", disse o TSE em comunicado. Procurada, a Meta respondeu que no comunicado divulgado pelo TSE estão todas as informações disponíveis. Os ministros do TSE, conforme a nota, mencionaram também o tema do uso dos canais de WhatsApp para promover conteúdo eleitoral. "A Meta informou que, de acordo com a política da empresa, as mensagens enviadas nos canais não são criptografadas", disse a empresa, segundo o TSE. De acordo com o TSE, a Meta se comprometeu ainda a empenhar os esforços necessários para vedar eventuais impulsionamentos de conteúdos de propaganda eleitoral feitos com moeda estrangeira.

item.title: Petey Halpin, dominant pitchers push Guardians to 2-1 ALCS lead over Rays
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Petey Halpin reacted to the most important hit of his young career by flipping his bat high into the sky. The rest of the Cleveland Guardians saved their wildest celebrations for the postgame.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Petey Halpin reacted to the most important hit of his young career by flipping his bat high into the sky. The rest of the Cleveland Guardians saved their wildest celebrations for the postgame. Halpin's go-ahead, two-run homer in the fifth inning off Griffin Jax was the difference in Game 3 of the American League Championship Series, giving Cleveland a 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday afternoon. The Guardians now lead the best-of-seven series 2-1. With the next two games at home, they could wrap up the pennant and book a trip to the World Series without a return to Florida. Halpin's first postseason home run traveled 385 feet over the fence in right, scoring Patrick Bailey to give the Guardians a 3-2 advantage. It was the first homer allowed by Jax since Sept. 9, prompting Halpin to send his bat comically airborne. "I thought I got more of it, I guess, and maybe I was a little tense, so I kind of threw it," Halpin said of the bat flip that ignited the non-sellout crowd of 30,101. "But it's only got to go a little bit over the wall, so that was cool." After Halpin gave AL Central champion Cleveland the lead, its pitching staff took over. Staff ace Gavin Williams and four relievers combined on a three-hitter, striking out 13 to raise their total to 102, an MLB record through eight postseason games. Williams (2-0) struck out nine over five innings, allowing two runs on two hits and a walk. The right-hander leads all postseason pitchers with 33 strikeouts in just 16 2/3 innings over four appearances. "I keep telling myself, 'Don't let the moment get too big,'" Williams said. "I've just got to keep the same routine and keep doing the same thing and I'll be good. "Everybody here is just gritty. That's the big thing. And knowing what you need to do in the right situations." Cade Smith pitched a perfect final 1 1/3 innings for his second save of the series. Daniel Espino, Erik Sabrowski and Hunter Gaddis also saw action as Cleveland began a three-game homestand in the series. Jax (0-1) worked four-plus innings, giving up three runs on five hits. The right-hander struck out two and walked a pair, but was left lamenting his lack of control on the sinker that Halpin sent over the fence. "He does a good job handling off-speed, so it was the right pitch," Jax said. "Just the wrong location." Tampa Bay took a 2-1 lead in the fourth on Chandler Simpson's two-run triple to right. Yandy Diaz and Victor Mesa Jr. scored on the hit that landed just inside the foul line, making Simpson 3-for-6 in his career against Williams. "It was a real good fastball, but I was ready for that," Simpson said. "I got a good pitch that I got the barrel on. The fact that we were down at the time, it gave us a lot of momentum." The Rays' three hits were their fewest in an ALCS game in three appearances. Their 2-1 series deficit is the first time they have trailed in the round after three games. Williams, who carried a no-hitter into the sixth in Game 5 of the AL Division Series against the Chicago White Sox, retired the first nine batters before Diaz doubled leading off the fourth. "Look, we're not a team that strikes out a lot, but I think our swings have actually been pretty good," Diaz said through a translator. "We just need to put the ball in play." Nathaniel Lowe doubled in the second, driving in Jo Adell to put Cleveland up 1-0. Adell had been called out on strikes by umpire Bill Miller, but challenged it and drew a walk. Diaz appeared in his franchise postseason-record 31st game for the Rays. Jax, an Air Force Reserve captain, became the first pitcher to graduate from a United States service academy and start a playoff game. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: Brazil candidates focus fiscal plans on voter-friendly measures before runoff
item.description: As Brazil's presidential runoff campaign enters its final stretch, both candidates are focusing plans for fiscal adjustments on politically palatable measures, reinforcing economists' views that strategies to curb the country's rising debt burden will only come to light after the election.
item.dc:creator: Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: As Brazil's presidential runoff campaign enters its final stretch, both candidates are focusing plans for fiscal adjustments on politically palatable measures, reinforcing economists' views that strategies to curb the country's rising debt burden will only come to light after the election. The country's gross debt has risen more than 10 percentage points during President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's current term, [USN:L1N45M0ES TEXT:"reaching"] 82.9% of gross domestic product (GDP), as the leftist incumbent seeks reelection after unexpectedly trailing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in the first round earlier this month. Right-wing Bolsonaro entered the race [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"promising"] a faster fiscal adjustment, targeting a 1.5% of GDP improvement in the primary balance within 18 months to trigger a confidence shock and lower borrowing costs. Long-term interest rates have [USN:L1N45R06Y TEXT:"fallen sharply"] since Bolsonaro's first-round victory, reflecting investor optimism about a potential change in government, although his campaign has yet to explain how such an adjustment would be delivered. Lula's campaign has also pledged fiscal consolidation, albeit at a slower pace, while saying that spending cuts should not fall on lower-income Brazilians, a message that has defined the president's economic agenda. With polls [USN:S0N45907Z TEXT:"showing"] Bolsonaro ahead by a narrow margin, both campaigns have stuck to politically safe fiscal proposals, sidestepping measures that would tackle the structural causes of Brazil's worsening fiscal outlook, analysts say. Economists broadly agree that the main challenge lies in the rapid growth of mandatory spending and an increasingly rigid budget. The federal government's discretionary spending accounted for only about 7.6% of total expenditures last year, versus 14.2% in 2000, when Brazil's Federal Budget Panel series began. Bolsonaro's economic adviser Daniella Marques rejected suggestions that a future administration would reduce social benefits, saying pensions and welfare programs would be untouched. "You can make the government work by cutting its own excesses," Marques told broadcaster Band on Wednesday, pointing to things like cuts in political appointments and ministries, among other measures. Lula's running mate Geraldo Alckmin has argued fiscal consolidation should focus on tackling campaign funding and outsized salaries earned by some public-sector workers. Neither campaign has confronted the deeper reforms required to stabilize debt, said Rafaela Vitoria, chief economist at Brazilian lender Inter. "There is no short-term magic solution," she said. "The debate on structural measures is extremely difficult during an election campaign because they are unpopular." Gradual adjustment remains feasible, Vitoria said, adding that discussions over benefit indexation rules, mandatory spending and overlapping social programs will likely have to wait until after the election.

item.title: Report: CFP nearing deal to expand to 24 teams in 2027
item.description: The College Football Playoff is nearing a deal to double its number of participating teams from 12 to 24, according to rights holder ESPN.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The College Football Playoff is nearing a deal to double its number of participating teams from 12 to 24, according to rights holder ESPN. The new format would come into effect in 2027 and is pending final approvals, the network reported on Thursday. "Constructive discussions with ESPN continued this week," read a statement from the CFP late Thursday. "We have enjoyed a strong partnership with ESPN since our inception and are appreciative of the productive dialogue we have had throughout the negotiating period and continuing over the last several days. We will provide additional updates on the matters of future format and media rights when appropriate." The playoff's quarterfinals and semifinals are expected to still belong to the New Year's Six bowl games (Rose, Fiesta, Sugar, Peach, Orange, Cotton) within the proposed new format, while the national championship game will likely remain in January. The CFP has used a 12-team format since 2024. From 2014 through 2023, just four teams competed in the postseason event. In March 2024, the CFP and ESPN agreed to a six-year, $7.8 billion contract, giving the network sole media rights through the 2031 season. After months of studying the pros and cons of expansion, the playoff's management committee moved forward with official discussions in September, which are ongoing. In the proposed plan, the top eight seeds receive byes, and seeds 9-16 host seeds 17-24 in the first round. The top eight then host the first-round winners. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season
item.description: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal, Rajendra Jadhav
item.content:encoded: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises. The notices from the fund houses, including Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund, did not cite a reason for the move. There is no restriction on redemptions from these funds. The decision was taken following a nudge from the Securities and Exchange Board of India, according to a mutual fund executive familiar with the discussions. Two bullion industry officials confirmed the halt had followed discussions with the market regulator. The sources declined to be identified as they are not permitted to comment on discussions with the regulator. A spokesperson for SEBI did not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours. The [USN:L1N45X01Q TEXT:"Indian rupee has been under pressure this year"] due to a surge in global oil prices, which have inflated the country's import bill, and heavy selling by foreign investors in Indian equities. Strong demand for gold has further weighed on the currency, prompting the government to raise import duties on gold and silver earlier this year. India, the world's largest consumer of silver and second-largest consumer of gold, relies on imports to meet most of its demand, a dependence that can sometimes widen its trade deficit. Gold imports fell to $1.8 billion in September, from $2.3 billion in August. However, Indians will celebrate Dussehra in October and Diwali in early November, when buying gold is considered auspicious. Inflows into gold and silver ETFs surged during last year's festive season as investors turned to precious metals amid lackluster stock market returns. The move is surprising, as gold and silver imports have fallen sharply over the past two months from a year earlier and have not contributed to the trade deficit, said a dealer at a private bank that supplies bullion to ETFs. "It looks more like a precautionary measure to avoid a surge in imports in October," the dealer said.

item.title: India markets regulator partly reverses derivative settlement rules after pushback
item.description: India's markets regulator said on Thursday it would use volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) from the final 30 minutes of regular trading to settle expiring stock and index derivatives contracts, reversing its decision to use closing auction prices.
item.dc:creator: Jayshree Pyasi, Bharath Rajeswaran, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: India's markets regulator said on Thursday it would use volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) from the final 30 minutes of regular trading to settle expiring stock and index derivatives contracts, reversing its decision to use closing auction prices. The closing auction session (CAS) will continue to determine the closing prices of applicable cash-equity securities, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said in a circular. CAS, implemented by SEBI from August 3, had triggered a backlash from traders after sharp swings in stock and index levels during the close. Erratic movements in the expiring derivatives contracts propelled traders to pull back on volumes. Reuters [USN:L1N45R0C2 TEXT:"reported"] last week that SEBI was considering reverting to 30-minute VWAP-based settlements for expiring derivatives contracts. The changes will be effective from December 7. CAS will operate as a separate 10-minute session from 3:30 p.m. to 3:40 p.m. on all trading days. Order entry will close randomly between 3:38 p.m. and 3:40 p.m. Traders can enter both limit and market orders from 3:31 p.m. to 3:36 p.m., after which they may place only limit orders. A market order is executed immediately at the best available price, while a limit order is executed only at the investor's specified price or better. Expiring index derivatives will cease trading at 3:30 p.m. on expiry days. Stock derivatives will continue to trade until 3:45 p.m. on all trading days, including expiry days. The cash-market post-close session will run from 3:50 p.m. to 4 p.m., with trades executed at the closing price.

item.title: FBI, US Postal Service investigate suspicious mailings to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The FBI said some of the letters contained an unknown substance. The investigation come less than three weeks before the midterms, which will determine control of the US Congress, as the Postal Service prepares to handle millions of mailed ballots. Spokespeople for Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, Alex Padilla, a California Democrat, and Chris Murphy, a Connecticut Democrat, all said the US Postal Service intercepted letters containing a suspicious substance mailed to their offices. "This incident is a stark reminder of the very real dangers facing those who serve the public and who help administer our elections," Padilla said in a statement. The US House of Representatives sergeant at arms, the House's chief law enforcement officer, told staff in an email seen by Reuters that some public officials had received letters containing suspicious white powder substances. Brendan Donahue, a deputy chief inspector with the US Postal Inspection Service, said some suspicious letters had been intercepted and that an investigation was ongoing. "We are committed to protecting our nation's election officials from threatening and dangerous mail. Any threat or attack on an election official is unacceptable," Donahue told reporters. The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors said late on Wednesday a series of suspicious letters was sent to state election offices. Letters bound for several state election offices were intercepted before they were delivered, including in Pennsylvania, Ohio and Idaho. The Wisconsin Elections Commission said on Thursday it received a suspicious letter with an unidentified powdery substance that was deemed not hazardous. "Let this be very clear: this incident will not shake us,” said Meagan Wolfe, the state’s chief election official. An email to Senate staff said suspicious letters could have postmarks that do not match the return address and included an image of an envelope with a return address labeled "DSA" and a New York City address. POSTAL SERVICE PLANS NEW MEASURES Earlier on Thursday, US Postmaster General David Steiner said USPS was "absolutely ready" to handle millions of ballots for the midterm elections. USPS said this month it would take "extraordinary measures" for the 2026 election, including extending hours at some retail locations and expediting handling, extra deliveries and special pickups of ballots. On September 14, the US Supreme Court declined to let USPS enforce a rule targeting mail-in ballots, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump's effort to restrict voting by mail. USPS said it would not enforce the rule under the order. The agency adopted the measure after Trump issued a March executive order aimed at tightening rules governing mail voting. In 2024, USPS delivered 99.2 million ballots to and from voters in the presidential election. About 30% of votes were cast by mail in the November 2024 presidential election, down from 46% in 2020. Trump's fellow Republicans are locked in a tight battle to retain control of Congress in the midterms. Democratic voters disproportionately use mail-in ballots, according to various surveys, so restricting them could benefit Republicans. Under the rule that was blocked, states would have had to provide lists of mail-ballot recipients to USPS and use agency-approved outbound and return ballot mail envelopes outfitted with unique barcodes. The Postal Service could then have refused to send out ballots that did not comply or were associated with voters not appearing on the lists.

item.title: US delays small imports rule that raised alarm over prescription drug costs
item.description: The US government has delayed by 90 days implementation of new customs requirements for small international mail shipments, a move that should forestall higher prices for imported prescription drugs and other products for inflation-weary Americans until after the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: The US government has delayed by 90 days implementation of new customs requirements for small international mail shipments, a move that should forestall higher prices for imported prescription drugs and other products for inflation-weary Americans until after the November midterm elections . The US Customs and Border Protection rule targets the [USN:L1N44A13F TEXT:"de minimis tariffs exemption"], which has eased requirements for shipments under $800. The rule aimed to speed up implementation of changes authorized by US lawmakers as part of President Donald Trump's spending and tax-cut bill, which are due to take effect in July 2027. The agency said on Wednesday it has pushed the mandatory compliance date for a new mail entry process to January 20, 2027, from October 22. That prior deadline was just 12 days before the November 3 elections in which US households' affordability woes are a central issue dogging Trump's Republican Party with control of Congress up for grabs. It said there would be no changes to international mail entry procedures before then. The process requires electronic filing for postal shipments subject to Section 201, 232 or 301 duties, or under the jurisdiction of a partner government agency such as the US Food and Drug Administration. It also involves a customs bond. As the October 22 deadline approached, patient advocates and industry groups had warned the rule's data and bonding requirements could cause delays, refusals or added costs for personal drug orders. IMPACT ON PHARMA The FDA officially bars individuals from importing foreign prescription drugs, but it has discretion in limited circumstances. Some Americans order medicines from other countries like Canada, where the cost of drugs can be sharply lower. The Canadian International Pharmacy Association has said most routine personal orders from licensed foreign pharmacies could be disrupted. A separate letter signed by 71 members of Congress, led by Democratic Representatives Jan Schakowsky of Illinois and Wisconsin's Mark Pocan, asked agencies to delay the procedures for prescription medicines unless personal-use drugs were assured. “For patients concerned about losing access to lower-cost prescriptions from abroad, this delay is a welcome reprieve, but not a permanent solution," said Merith Basey, CEO of Patients For Affordable Drugs. "Until patients in the US can get access to the prescription drugs they need at prices they can afford, disrupting existing personal-importation practices risks an important safety valve.” The Department of Health and Human Services referred questions to CBP, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether personal-use exemptions are planned. CBP said the extension gives importers, brokers and logistics providers more time to update processes, helps avoid disruptions and will close gaps that have been exploited by smugglers. CBP's announcement did not mention medicines, and the rule does not name them.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis hit palace in Aden, coalition details attacks on Saudi infrastructure
item.description: Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people, the government said, as the Saudi-led coalition listed dozens of Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people, the government said, as the Saudi-led coalition listed dozens of Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in recent weeks. The attack was the first in the current conflict between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia on Aden's Al-Maashiq palace, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed and internationally recognised government. The conflict is a new theatre in the wider regional war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Yemen's prime minister and cabinet members were safe following the attack, Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said. Witnesses told Reuters they heard loud booms near the palace. Yemen's cabinet said the attack involved missiles and drones. Yemen's health minister Qasim Buhaibeh said five people were killed and 16 wounded in what he described as a Houthi attack on the government's official headquarters at the presidential complex. The casualties included guards and civilian employees. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said its fighters had bombed what he described as the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden, as part of the group's declared policy of targeting "Saudi reinforcements wherever they were located". The Houthi-run news agency SABA said the headquarters was run by Saudi officers and that there were weapons depots there. Reuters could not independently verify the claims. Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces resumed last month, and aid agencies [USN:L6N4600ML TEXT:"have warned"] of rapidly worsening conditions in Yemen. Last week, government forces launched a campaign to recapture areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping artery. War broke out in Yemen in 2014 when [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"the Houthis"] seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south. A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year. In that phase of the conflict Houthi fighters and allied forces briefly seized Al-Maashiq palace during a battle for Aden, before withdrawing. COALITION SAYS HOUTHIS ARE GETTING MISSILES, FAST BOATS As Saudi Arabia backs government forces, the Houthis [USN:L1N4610L5 TEXT:"have been firing"] ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a [USN:L1N46108L TEXT:"pressure point"] in the wider war [USN:L6N45Y0GN TEXT:"and threatening"] its ambitious economic plans. On Thursday, the Saudi-led military coalition said the Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of such sites, highlighting the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure. The governing council of the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization condemned the recent attacks on civilian airports, aircraft, and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki told reporters that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. The airport is one of Saudi Arabia's main international aviation hubs. The coalition said Houthi attacks on Abha airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border had killed three people and wounded 28. Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats. Iran [USN:L1N43P0D6 TEXT:"has provided"] weapons, money and training to the Houthis, although Tehran has officially denied arming them in violation of a UN arms embargo. Maliki also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen's mountainous areas, calling on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure. Shortly afterwards, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority issued early-warning alerts throughout Thursday over potential threats in the cities of Najran and Jizan, as well as the wider Najran and Jazan regions, before later saying the danger had passed. The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday that it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the southwestern Saudi Arabian city of Khamis Mushait, and another launched towards the country's southern region.

item.title: Huracán Trudy cobra fuerza frente a costa de México golpeada por lluvias
item.description: El huracán Trudy se seguía fortaleciendo el jueves sobre el océano Pacífico, a medida que enfilaba hacia la costa occidental de México, amenazando con dejar más lluvias y fuertes vientos en una zona castigada en las últimas semanas por varios ciclones tropicales que dejaron inundaciones y víctimas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se seguía fortaleciendo el jueves sobre el océano Pacífico, a medida que enfilaba hacia la costa occidental de México, amenazando con dejar más lluvias y fuertes vientos en una zona castigada en las últimas semanas por varios ciclones tropicales que dejaron inundaciones y víctimas. A las 17.00 hora local (2300 GMT), el ciclón se ubicaba a unos 380 kilómetros al sur-suroeste de la ciudad portuaria Acapulco, en el estado Guerrero, y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 150 kilómetros por hora (km/h), con ráfagas más fuertes, mientras avanzaba hacia el norte-noroeste a 9 km/h, según el más reciente reporte del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). Se espera que Trudy se siga intensificando rápidamente hasta convertirse cerca del mediodía del viernes en un huracán de categoría 4 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson. Un ciclón de ese nivel puede soplar vientos máximos sostenidos de hasta 250 km/h y causar daños generalizados en estructuras protectoras, desplome de tejados en edificios pequeños, erosión de bancales y playas e inundaciones en terrenos interiores. "Si Trudy se intensifica como se pronostica, los fuertes vientos cerca de su centro generarán olas peligrosamente altas en altamar. El oleaje se extenderá hacia afuera, amenazando tanto a embarcaciones pequeñas como a grandes buques", advirtió AccuWeather, una compañía estadounidense de servicios comerciales de pronóstico del tiempo. Si bien no se prevé que Trudy toque tierra, descargará lluvias torrenciales y dejará fuertes ráfagas de viento y oleaje peligroso en la franja costera que va desde el conocido destino turístico Acapulco hasta Puerto Vallarta, pasando por los dos mayores puertos del país: Manzanillo y Lázaro Cárdenas, puerta de entrada principal para mercancías provenientes de Asia. Por la tarde del jueves, pescadores recogían sus embarcaciones en Acapulco y las aseguraban en la arena en previsión de tempestades. Autoridades exhortaron a la población a extremar precauciones y cerraron algunos puertos pesqueros y turísticos a la navegación de embarcaciones menores. "La gravedad de las condiciones en la costa mexicana provocadas por Trudy dependerá de si el ojo del huracán alcanza la costa o si, por el contrario, la tormenta roza la línea costera. Una diferencia de trayectoria de entre 80 y 160 kilómetros podría tener consecuencias muy diferentes", agregó AccuWeather. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano fue golpeada por los huracanes [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo"] y [USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:"Simón"]. Si bien este último tampoco tocó tierra, sigue activo, aunque como tormenta tropical, frente a la costa centroccidental del país.

item.title: Market selloff, rising rates test AI data centre deal boom
item.description: A market selloff is forcing companies driving the global AI boom to delay fundraising plans or pay more for capital as investors demand proof they can absorb rising interest rates and computing-power costs.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Kane Wu, Clare Jim
item.content:encoded: A [USN:L6N4610C5 TEXT:"market selloff"] is forcing companies driving the global AI boom to delay fundraising plans or pay more for capital as investors demand proof they can absorb rising interest rates and computing-power costs. The shift comes as investors reassess whether the companies racing to build the infrastructure underpinning artificial intelligence can generate returns that justify soaring spending on computing power, land and energy. In the past week alone, as AI-related stocks have weakened and the debt of data-centre operator [USN:L8N4610AR TEXT:"CoreWeave"] has slumped towards distressed prices, listings for a Blackstone-backed [USN:L4N45Z0H4 TEXT:"AirTrunk"] REIT, Nvidia-backed [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"Firmus"] and SoftBank-backed [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"SB Energy"] have either been pulled or paused. The increased scrutiny is not derailing investment in the sector, analysts said, but it is forcing investors to distinguish more sharply between business models and levels of execution risk. "The conversation has shifted from growth at any cost to a much sharper focus on quality," said Harry Evans, a partner at law firm Freshfields. Evans said deal activity could hold up through next year, thanks to a strong pipeline. Recent listing setbacks, however, show investors are becoming more discerning about valuations, leverage and business models. M&A involving Asian data centres is still on track for a record year, reaching $21.3 billion as of Tuesday, according to Dealogic data, more than double the $10 billion recorded in all of 2025. Debt financing has also remained strong, with syndicated loans and bond issuance totalling $22.3 billion so far this year. Equity capital market fundraising for the sector, however, is down, at $5.4 billion so far this year, a 4.6% drop from the same period in 2025. "General thoughts with IPOs are that they often seek 'hype', as they're largely looking for oversubscription," said Nicholas Tuan, director, APAC Advisory Services at real estate services firm Savills. "There may not be fundamental asset value when you peel it all back." Firmus, which had aimed to raise $5 billion in what would have been Australia's second-largest stock market listing, struggled to convince investors it could deliver on ambitious revenue projections while carrying about $30 billion of debt. Nuclear services company [USN:L4N4581N6 TEXT:"Holtec"] cited a "[USN:L4N45H14U TEXT:"perfect storm"]", driven mainly by uncertainty around data-centre demand, when it pulled its US listing last month. HIGHER RATES TEST VALUATIONS Higher borrowing costs are at the heart of the new scrutiny. Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields posted their sharpest quarterly rise this century last month, prompting investors to take a closer look at whether projected revenues can support growing debt burdens, bankers said. Gary Goh, CEO of Sprint DC Consulting, an Asia-Pacific data centre consultancy firm based in Kuala Lumpur, warned higher financing costs could lead to sharp valuation corrections. Valuations can vary widely depending on whether they are based on existing customer contracts or future projections, and whether capital expenditure requirements are fully reflected, said a banker who advises data-centre investors. "There is not remotely enough data centres built for the demand," said the banker, who was not authorised to speak publicly. "Investors are still going in but the question is at what valuation." Investors are also paying closer attention to execution risks. Beyond higher power and water costs, developers face [USN:L1N45M0CN TEXT:"growing opposition"] in some markets over electricity use, noise and environmental concerns, adding to regulatory uncertainty around new projects. Securing suitable land and power supplies is becoming more difficult in some jurisdictions, said a person at a US-based firm that invests in Asian data-centre platforms, adding that the company had tightened its underwriting criteria because of geopolitical and policy risks. To be sure, major transactions are still [USN:L6N460198 TEXT:"moving ahead"]. Singapore-based DayOne is expected to go public as soon as November, seeking to raise up to $5 billion, Reuters [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"reported"] in September. DayOne did not immediately respond to a request for comment. AirTrunk, despite postponing a planned REIT listing, is nearing a deal to sell its Johor data centre in Malaysia to a group of investors including local pension fund KWAP at a valuation of about $1 billion, according to two people familiar with the matter. Bain Capital has also received final bids for at least 40% of its pan-Asian platform Bridge Data Centres in a deal that could value the business at around $5 billion, according to two people with knowledge of the process. AirTrunk's backer Blackstone and Bain Capital declined to comment. KWAP said it was not in a position to comment. Still, investors are likely to differentiate between established wholesale operators with long-term customer commitments and stable revenue, and higher-risk "neoclouds" and "AI-campus builders", said John Dinsdale, chief analyst at TechInsights. "The question for investors is less whether demand will expand than which business models and companies will be best placed to capture that growth sustainably."

item.title: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
item.description: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday. Its services gave Israel's Candiru — a spyware company [USN:L1N2RU186 TEXT:"blacklisted by the US government"] — as well as other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google (GOOGL.O) , Comcast (CMCSA.O) , Russia's Yandex and others, according to separate reports from Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant. The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns. "The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat," Wolfie Christl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters. "For states, the private sector, civil society and everyone else alike." Discover-Tech's online ads — often for ordinary products such as phones or earbuds — reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen Lab said. Users who visited sites or used apps with the malicious ads could be identified and tracked by Discover-Tech, which would sometimes also try to extract phone numbers from some smartphone users, the researchers said. Ads only needed to load on a website for the spying to occur. Some ads would be used to help plant spyware from Candiru on users' devices, both research groups said, though Confiant said that ads it tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech's overall volume. MALICIOUS ADS SHOWN IN HUNDREDS OF SENSITIVE NETWORKS Confiant cofounder Jerome Dangu said Discover-Tech was pumping out at least 10 million ads per day all around the world and that data-sharing arrangements — called cookie matching — allowed it to track people even beyond the reach of its advertisements. "Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech," Dangu said. Discover-Tech, which was founded in 2020, did not return messages left via its contact form. A LinkedIn message and emails sent to its chief executive, Dekel Boni, were not returned. Reuters' attempts to reach Candiru's owners were similarly unsuccessful. The US Commerce Department blacklisted Candiru in 2021 for [USN:L1N2RU186 TEXT:"allegedly supplying spyware"] that was used to maliciously target government officials, journalists, activists and academics. Citizen Lab said a powerful form of Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech's ads had been used to compromise 45 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025, something it said it was able to confirm because the media group had shared its network logs with the group. In a statement, Al Jazeera said it "condemns the spyware attacks targeting a number of its staff" and that it was taking steps to protect its employees and its systems. "Those responsible must be held accountable," it said. Dangu of Confiant said that the malicious ads had been shown to users in "hundreds of networks in sensitive categories," including the Pentagon, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court. He also said that some regions, like the Palestinian territories, were particularly saturated by the Israeli firm's ads. "You go to almost any site in Palestine — any site — you find a Discover-Tech ad. It gives them a very complete visibility on the digital activities of an entire country," he said. Citizen Lab also said it had similar evidence showing the malicious ads were shown to people in the United Nations, NATO, the European Commission, and more than a dozen national governments. Other networks the ads appeared in included chip-related firms such as Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Sandisk (SNDK.O) , Broadcom (AVGO.O) , and Micron (MU.O) , as well as several media organizations in Mexico, Israel, and Europe that were not identified. In addition to identifying Candiru and a couple of other surveillance vendors, Citizen Lab said it was able to glean some details about where Discover-Tech's users might be based because the firm inadvertently exposed its authentication logs to the internet, showing people logging in from internet protocol addresses in Israel, Europe, and the Gulf. MEASURES AGAINST DISCOVER-TECH TAKEN Discover-Tech is now being frozen out of parts of the online ad market. Google said in a statement that it had collaborated with Citizen Lab and Confiant's investigation and kicked Discover-Tech off its ad platforms "for systematically violating our policies." IAB Europe, the European-level association for the digital marketing and advertising ecosystem, said in an email that Discover-Tech had been suspended from its list of globally approved vendors last week after an audit identified policy violations. Comcast ad tech subsidiary Beeswax removed Discover-Tech from its platform "following recent activity," Comcast said in a statement. Yandex did not return Reuters messages seeking comment. Advertising-driven surveillance is increasingly being seen as a national security threat. Earlier this year, the Pentagon said it had received reports that US forces deployed to war zones had been [USN:L6N4240BC TEXT:"targeted using location data"] harvested by ad tech firms and data brokers. Branches of the military have since [USN:L6N44V02G TEXT:"disabled ad tracking"] on some devices.

item.title: Tesla unveils next generation Roadster sports EV with SpaceX thrusters
item.description: Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster equipped with thrusters on Thursday, nearly nine years after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car and said it would start production in 2028.
item.dc:creator: Abhirup Roy
item.content:encoded: Tesla (TSLA.O) unveiled a redesigned Roadster equipped with thrusters on Thursday, nearly nine years after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car and said it would start production in 2028. Tesla demonstrated the two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX, showing it driving upside down on a ramp using a suction system and turning in the air and landing using in-built thrusters. The use and legality of such features on public roads were not immediately clear. Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially." But the car still carries symbolic weight. "Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month. Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of $200,000 for the vehicle. Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed a "Performance" version of the vehicle requiring a $50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a $250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla says is "invite only", is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system". The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 miles per hour in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 230 mph, Musk said at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas. Tesla revealed a prototype of the car in 2017 and said then that deliveries would begin in 2020. Musk had set high expectations in 2017, saying a four-seat Roadster would travel 620 miles (1,000 km) on a single charge. Goldstein expects Tesla to sell around 2,000 Roadsters a year — a fraction of the 1.6 million vehicles Tesla sold last year. The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever EV and used a Lotus Elise chassis. It helped change the world's view of what an electric vehicle could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans. The reveal of the second-generation Roadster also comes amid a sharp shift in Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers. This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab - a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors.

item.title: AstraZeneca strikes $40 million AI drug discovery deal with insitro
item.description: AstraZeneca has teamed up with artificial intelligence biotech company insitro to discover and develop new treatments for difficult to treat liver and heart conditions, the British drugmaker said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Wingrove
item.content:encoded: AstraZeneca (AZN.L) has teamed up with artificial intelligence biotech company insitro to discover and develop new treatments for difficult to treat liver and heart conditions, the British drugmaker said on Thursday. Under the agreement, AstraZeneca will pay $40 million up front, with California-based insitro eligible for up to about $1.46 billion in potential development and commercial milestones, as well as a single-digit percentage of future sales in royalties. The multi-year collaboration will focus on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a severe liver disease, and cardiomyopathies, a group of diseases that affect the heart muscle. Both have historically lacked effective therapies because researchers have struggled to pinpoint their root biological drivers, the drugmaker said. Insitro will use its "Virtual Human" AI platform, which combines lab-grown cell models and machine learning, to identify causal disease biology and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development-candidate stage. AstraZeneca will then run and fund future clinical trials. The deal builds on insitro's expansion across the pharmaceuticals industry. The biotech company recently expanded its partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY.N) to advance a broader portfolio of targets for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). It also teamed up with Eli Lilly (LLY.N) to build AI models that predict pharmacological properties of small molecules in living organisms. "Choosing the new targets that we want to put into our discovery pipeline is one of the hardest things we do across research and development," Sharon Barr, executive vice president of biopharmaceuticals R&D at AstraZeneca, told Reuters. "By the time we read about a new pathway or target (in major scientific journals), it is no longer novel. It's in the public domain and we're already a few steps too late. But when we identify these unique connections early and test them in cellular systems, we're ahead of the game." Barr added that pairing AI tools with experienced scientists allows the company to test fewer molecules in the lab, reduce guesswork and speed the search for effective medicines.

item.title: S&P 500 ends higher as traders shift from AI to healthcare
